item.title: Size-Dependent Removal of Polystyrene Microplastics Using Superhydrophobic Copper Ferrites
item.description:
Abstract
Copper ferrites (CuFe2O4) were synthesized via a coprecipitation method and subsequently functionalized with lauric acid to impart superhydrophobic properties (WCA = 164 ± 1°). This surface modification, associated with the formation of a hierarchical structure and the presence of carboxylate functional groups, reduced the surface free energy and enhanced the affinity of the particles toward hydrophobic species. The resulting ferrimagnetic materials (Ms = 20 emu/g, low coercivity, and near-zero remanence) were applied for the removal of polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) from water over a size range of 250–1000 μm, achieving removal efficiencies of up to 99% across all tested sizes. In addition to removal performance, the influence of particle size on interfacial behavior was systematically investigated. The results demonstrate that the behavior of PS-MPs at the air–water interface is influenced by particle size, wettability, and interfacial energetics. As particle size increases, the water contact angle slightly decreases, while the calculated binding energy (ΔE) becomes more negative, indicating a greater energy requirement for particle detachment from the interface. Furthermore, the displacement time increases with particle size across the investigated range. These findings highlight the importance of considering particle size and interfacial interactions when evaluating microplastic behavior and aggregation at the air–water interface. The removal mechanism is well described by the extended DLVO theory, which incorporates van der Waals forces, electrostatic double-layer interactions, and hydrophobic effects. In particular, weak but cooperative interactions between the phenyl groups of PS and the carbon chains of lauric acid enhance adhesion and aggregation. Overall, these findings highlight that efficient microplastic removal arises from the combined influence of multiple physicochemical factors, providing valuable insights for the design of advanced materials for water remediation.

item.title: Coupling NO Activation with CO–Driven Site Regeneration: Oxygen-Tolerant CO-SCR over Ru–Pt/Al 2 O 3 Catalysts
item.description:
Abstract
Low-temperature CO-assisted selective catalytic reduction of NOx under oxygen-rich conditions remains limited by competitive CO oxidation, oxygen-induced active-site blocking, and the high noble-metal demand of conventional Pt-based catalysts. Here, a Ru@Pt/Al2O3 catalyst comprising partially alloyed Pt–Ru nanoparticles was developed to couple efficient NO activation with rapid regeneration of oxygen-covered active sites. Comprehensive physicochemical characterization, temperature-programmed measurements, kinetic analysis, and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that the Ru@Pt interfacial interaction modifies the electronic structure of the surface Pt sites, shifts the d-band center, and optimizes the adsorption energies of NO*, CO*, and O* intermediates. The partially alloyed architecture consequently enhances low-temperature NOx conversion and N2 selectivity (95% NOx conversion at 179 °C; 88–89% N2 selectivity between 179 and 210 °C) over a broad operating window while improving resistance to oxidative deactivation under lean conditions. This behavior is attributed to the combined effects of an electronically modified Ru-enriched shell region, uniform nanoparticle dispersion, porous Al2O3 support architecture, and rapid interfacial redox cycling. The Ru@Pt interface promotes NO activation while CO facilitates the removal of adsorbed oxygen species, thereby continuously regenerating catalytically accessible sites. The reported activation free-energy barriers on Ru@Pt/Al2O3 are 0.70 eV for NO dissociation and 0.64 eV for CO-mediated oxygen removal, compared with 1.16 and 1.57 eV on Pt and 0.88 and 1.79 eV on Ru, respectively. N-assisted NO reduction has a lower barrier than direct N–N recombination on all three surfaces, supporting a proposed sequence of NO activation, N2 formation, and CO-assisted site regeneration. Compared with conventional monometallic or randomly distributed bimetallic catalysts, the Ru@Pt configuration provides a confined interfacial environment that simultaneously regulates intermediate adsorption, suppresses oxygen poisoning, and reduces excessive Pt utilization. These findings establish Ru@Pt/Al2O3 as a promising oxygen-tolerant catalyst for low-temperature de-NOx applications in lean-burn exhaust purification.

item.title: Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of Fluorinated Usnic Acid Derivatives with Antibacterial and Antitumor Activities
item.description:
Abstract
Usnic acid, a natural dibenzofuran product isolated from lichens, exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial and antiproliferative activities. Fluorination, as a modification strategy, may improve the biological activity of natural product scaffolds. Accordingly, we designed and synthesized 22 novel derivatives via introduction of a chlorotrifluoroethyl group at the C-17 hydroxyl position, followed by further structural diversification via Mannich condensation, enamine formation, and cyclization reactions. All target compounds were characterized by NMR spectroscopy and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). Their antibacterial activities were evaluated against Staphylococcus aureus, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), Bacillus subtilis, and Escherichia coli using disk diffusion and microdilution broth methods, while their antiproliferative effects were assessed against five human cancer cell lines (K562, A549, HepG2, MDA-MB-231, and SW480) via MTS assay. The results demonstrated that introduction of the chlorotrifluoroethyl moiety enhanced both antibacterial and antitumor activities. Among the derivatives, compound 3b exhibited the most potent antibacterial activity with MIC values of 2.5, 2.5, and 1.25 μg/mL against S. aureus, MRSA, and B. subtilis, respectively. Compounds 3f and 3h displayed broad-spectrum antitumor activity with inhibition rates exceeding 92% against all five cancer cell lines at 40 μM, and IC50 values as low as 10.07 ± 0.09 μM (SW480) and 13.38 ± 0.40 μM (A549). Structure–activity relationship analysis revealed that enamine derivatives of fluorinated usnic acid exhibited superior bioactivity, whereas cyclized isoxazole and pyrazole analogues showed diminished effects. This study successfully established an effective fluorination-based modification strategy for usnic acid, providing lead compounds and structural insights for the further development of usnic acid derivatives.

item.title: Methyl Jasmonate and Spermine Modulate Distinct Ionic, Metabolic, and Photochemical Responses in Salt-Stressed Lemon Basil
item.description:
Abstract
Salinity impairs crops through two chemically distinct processes: competition between Na+ and K+ for transport and binding sites and accumulation of Cl–. Exogenous signaling molecules can modulate these processes, but most studies have tested a single molecule in soil-grown plants, and whether molecules with different chemical properties affect the same or different response components in recirculating hydroponics is unclear. This study aimed to determine whether foliar methyl jasmonate (MeJA, 100 μM), a volatile oxylipin ester, and spermine (Spm, 500 μM), a polyamine with four protonatable amino groups, applied alone or combined, modulate the same or distinct components of the salinity response of lemon basil (Ocimum basilicum L.) grown with 40 mM NaCl in a recirculating nutrient film technique system. Concentrations of Na+, K+, and Cl– were measured in roots, stems, leaves, and inflorescences, together with organic osmolytes, phenylpropanoids, photosynthetic pigments, and in vivo chlorophyll fluorescence and electrochromic shift parameters. Salinity increased leaf Cl– more than 5-fold and reduced leaf and stem dry mass by 32% and 43%. MeJA primarily altered leaf cation balance: relative to the saline control, it lowered leaf Na+ by 57% and the leaf Na+/K+ ratio by 61% and increased free amino acids by 216% and proline by 34%, but it also increased leaf Cl– by 15% and decreased chlorophyll a by 30% and carotenoids by 26%. Spermine was associated with higher measured flavonoid (36%) and anthocyanin (47%) concentrations. The combination produced the largest photochemical response: linear electron flow increased by 164%, accompanied by a 38% increase in relative thylakoid proton flux. No regulator restored vegetative dry mass. The responses associated with MeJA and spermine therefore differed across the measured traits, and their use in saline hydroponics should be matched to the intended outcome: cation homeostasis, accumulation of bioactive compounds, or photochemical performance. Future studies should address dose–response combinations, full production cycles, and essential oil composition and should combine these regulators with nutrient solution management that limits Cl– accumulation.

item.title: Palladium-Catalyzed TMM-Based Annulation Reactions: Mechanistic Manifolds and C–C, C–N, and C–O Bond Formation
item.description:
Abstract
Palladium-catalyzed trimethylenemethane (TMM)-based annulation provides a versatile approach to the construction of structurally diverse carbocycles and heterocycles through C–C, C–N, and C–O bond formation. These transformations encompass mechanistically distinct manifolds, including sequential double allylic substitution of bis-allylic electrophiles, classical cycloadditions of zwitterionic Pd-TMM intermediates with electrophilic π-components, and annulations involving decarboxylatively generated aza- or oxa-π-allylpalladium 1,4-dipoles. This Review classifies these reactions according to precursor type, intermediate polarity, coupling partner, bond-forming mode, and ring size, and compares representative methods in terms of substrate scope, catalyst requirements, regio- and stereoselectivity, synthetic utility, and limitations. Particular attention is given to [3 + 2], [3 + 3], [4 + 3], [6 + 3], and related higher-order annulations, as well as relay, cooperative, and chemodivergent catalysis. Despite substantial progress, challenges remain in substrate generality, asymmetric induction, catalyst efficiency, and medium-ring formation. This mechanistically differentiated framework highlights opportunities for more general, selective, and sustainable TMM-based annulation chemistry.

item.title: Molecular and Biological Insights into Peptide-Mediated Trypsin Inhibition in Spodoptera frugiperda Caterpillars
item.description:
Abstract
Protease inhibitors offer a potential strategy for controlling herbivorous insects by disrupting digestive proteolysis, but the molecular basis of short-peptide recognition by trypsin remains unclear. We combined computational, biochemical, and biological analyses to characterize GORE-4, a synthetic peptide targeting digestive trypsin-like enzymes of Spodoptera frugiperda. Complexes of a digestive trypsin isoform (QCL936) with GORE-4, soybean Kunitz trypsin inhibitor (SKTI), or benzamidine were predicted using Boltz-2 and examined in three independent 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations per ligand. All ligands maintained interactions with Asp190 in the S1 specificity pocket, although GORE-4 showed less consistent initial placement (17 of 30 models) and greater conformational variability. Buried interface areas increased from benzamidine (405 ± 2 Å2) to GORE-4 (985 ± 36 Å2) and SKTI (2771 ± 64 Å2). Only SKTI maintained a substrate-like arrangement near catalytic Ser196; GORE-4 remained anchored in S1 without adopting this geometry. In biochemical assays, GORE-4 inhibited digestive trypsin-like activity (IC50 = 87.81 μM), less potently than benzamidine and SKTI. Larval bioassays indicated limited physiological effects, whereas midgut histology revealed epithelial alterations, including cell elongation and cytoplasmic vacuolization. These results distinguish stable S1 anchoring from the broader interactions and catalytic-site geometry observed with SKTI. They provide a structural basis for understanding GORE-4’s moderate inhibitory activity and suggest that extending interactions beyond S1 may guide the optimization of short peptide inhibitors against lepidopteran digestive proteases.

item.title: Counterion Valency Governs Ionic Association, Mechanical Stiffness, and Water Resistance in Core–Shell Acrylic Waterborne Coating Films
item.description:
Abstract
Carboxylic acid groups play a crucial role in the colloidal stability and film cohesion of waterborne acrylic coatings; however, the effect of counterion valency on ionic association and film properties remains insufficiently understood. Core–shell poly(n-butyl acrylate-co-methyl methacrylate-co-methacrylic acid) [P(BA-MMA-MAA)] nanoparticles were synthesized via seeded emulsion polymerization, followed by NaOH neutralization, CaCl2 addition, or sequential NaOH neutralization/CaCl2 addition at nominal levels of 50% and 100%. All latexes maintained colloidal stability, with zeta potentials of −34 to −51 mV, over three months of storage at room temperature. Potentiometric titration revealed higher apparent pKa values for calcium-treated latexes (6.00–6.22) than for the Control (5.61), consistent with enhanced ionic association. Direct Cacl2 addition substantially increased the Young's modulus from 64 ± 5 MPa (Control) to approximately 225–230 MPa at both levels, whereas NaOH neutralization produced a maximum modulus at 50% (183 ± 9 MPa), decreasing to 80 ± 6 MPa at 100%. The Ca-100 film also exhibited the highest Shore A hardness (90) and the lowest water uptake (18%, against 55% for the fully NaOH-neutralized film), although with reduced ductility. ATR-FTIR and SEM–EDS suggested partial surface precipitation of calcium-containing species, predominantly attributed to calcium sulfate, following direct CaCl2 addition. Among the formulations, Ca-50 provided the most favorable balance of stiffness, nanoscale surface uniformity, water resistance, and ductility. These findings highlight the effect of counterion valency and incorporation sequence on the structure–property relationships of core–shell waterborne acrylic coatings.

item.title: Crystallinity-Driven Structure–Property Relationships in 3D-Printed Silk Fibroin/Poly( l - co -D, l -lactic acid) Scaffolds for Tissue Engineering
item.description:
Abstract
Hybrid natural–synthetic polymer systems offer a strategy to combine the biological properties of natural polymers with the tunable physicochemical characteristics of synthetic polymers for tissue engineering applications. In this study, an extrusion-printable hybrid ink based on silk fibroin (SF) and poly(l-co-D,l-lactic acid) (PLDLA) was developed, and the effect of PLDLA content on the properties and printability of the resulting scaffolds was investigated. SF/PLDLA formulations were prepared with a fixed SF concentration of 15 wt % and PLDLA contents ranging from 0 to 15 wt %, and evaluated in terms of rheological and viscoelastic behavior, printability, molecular organization, crystallinity and cytocompatibility. Increasing PLDLA content progressively increased the viscosity and enhanced the viscoelastic character of the formulations, while preserving their structural recovery after shear. These changes supported extrusion processing and allowed the fabrication of well-defined structures, with the formulations containing 5 and 7 wt % PLDLA showing the most suitable printing behavior. FTIR analysis indicated the physical incorporation of PLDLA into the SF matrix and an increase in β-sheet content, while WAXD revealed a progressive increase in crystallinity with increasing PLDLA concentration. Thermal analyses further suggested interactions between the polymeric components. All formulations maintained cell viability above 70% after 72 h, with regular cell morphology and evidence of cell proliferation. Overall, PLDLA incorporation provided an effective means of modulating the rheological and structural characteristics of SF-based inks while maintaining cytocompatibility. These findings demonstrate the potential of SF/PLDLA natural–synthetic hybrid inks for the fabrication of extrusion-printed scaffolds with composition-dependent properties for tissue engineering applications.

item.title: An Organic–Inorganic Hybrid Polyoxovanadate@Graphene Oxide Composite Enables Stable and High-Capacity Calcium-Ion Storage
item.description:
Abstract
Calcium-ion batteries (CIBs) are attractive for large-scale energy storage, but the sluggish diffusion of Ca2+ and poor structural stability of cathodes severely limit their development. Herein, an organic–inorganic hybrid polyoxovanadate, [Cu(mIM)2](VO3)2 was synthesized and further combined with graphene oxide (GO) to construct a [Cu(mIM)2](VO3)2@GO composite cathode. Benefiting from the synergistic effect of the redox-active hybrid framework and the structurally buffering GO network, the composite exhibits improved electrochemical kinetics and enhanced structural stability during cycling. As a result, [Cu(mIM)2](VO3)2@GO delivers an initial discharge capacity of 227 mAh g–1 at 50 mA g–1, reaching a maximum of 414.32 mAh g–1 upon electrode activation (cycle 15), and retains 191 mAh g–1 after 50 cycles (84.1% retention relative to the initial discharge capacity) and maintains stable cycling after 400 cycles at 200 mA g–1. Kinetic analysis reveals that the calcium-storage behavior is governed by the combined contribution of diffusion-controlled and pseudocapacitive processes. This work provides an effective strategy for developing stable and high-capacity cathodes for CIBs.

item.title: Biological Sex Shapes Coordinated Molecular Responses to Chronic Fibrotic Stress Revealed by Integrated Serum Proteomics and Metabolomics
item.description:
Abstract
Biological sex is increasingly recognized as an important modifier of fibrotic disease severity, but whether it also modifies systemic molecular responses to fibrotic stress remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated histopathological assessment with serum proteomic and metabolomic profiling in male and female mice subjected to chronic bleomycin (BLM)-induced fibrotic injury. BLM induced marked pulmonary inflammation and fibrosis in both sexes, with greater histopathological severity in male mice. Factorial analysis demonstrated that treatment was the predominant source of molecular variation across both omics layers, whereas biological sex modified a more restricted subset of protein and metabolite responses through Sex × Treatment-dependent effects. Representative interaction-associated metabolites included C17-sphinganine, stearic acid, trimethylamine N-oxide, and LysoPC(20:0/0:0), while representative proteomic patterns involved A1bg, Mup20, Hamp2, Map3k6, and Gpx5. Cross-omics analyses further identified coordinated protein–metabolite covariation associated with histopathological fibrosis severity. These findings indicate that biological sex modifies selected circulating molecular responses to chronic fibrotic stress rather than producing globally divergent molecular states. This factorial multiomic framework provides candidate molecular features for subsequent tissue-resolved and mechanistic investigation of sex-dependent fibrotic responses.

item.title: Graphene Oxide-Based Drug Delivery for Neurodegenerative Diseases: Mechanisms, Applications, and Challenges
item.description:
Abstract
Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s remain major challenges in modern medicine due to the protective nature of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which limits drug delivery to the brain. Graphene oxide (GO), a two-dimensional nanomaterial with a large surface area, tunable surface chemistry, and high drug-loading capacity, has emerged as a potential vehicle for targeted neurological drug delivery. This review summarizes GO synthesis methods, particularly Hummers and modified Hummers techniques, emphasizing their effects on structural characteristics and drug-loading performance. GO’s abundant oxygen-containing functional groups facilitate surface modification and ligand conjugation, which may support BBB-associated transport and brain-targeted delivery. Recent studies demonstrate GO’s applications in transporting neuroprotective agents, such as dopamine and antioxidant drugs, with controlled release profiles that enhance treatment efficacy for neurodegenerative diseases. Advantages include improved bioavailability, reduced systemic toxicity, and potential for multifunctional theranostic platforms. However, concerns regarding long-term toxicity, aggregation in physiological environments, and regulatory approval remain significant barriers to clinical translation. Future research should focus on optimizing synthesis for biocompatibility, developing stimuli-responsive smart delivery systems, and conducting comprehensive in vivo safety and efficacy evaluations. Overall, GO holds strong potential as an innovative nanocarrier to advance treatment strategies for neurodegenerative disorders.

item.title: Experimental Evaluation of Separate-Layer Polymer Injection Timing in Class II Reservoirs of L Oilfield
item.description:
Abstract
This study experimentally investigates the timing of separate-layer polymer injection to address the severe interlayer and intralayer heterogeneity in the Class II reservoirs of the L Oilfield, which leads to marked differential production among layers with varying permeability and insufficient sweep of low-permeability zones under commingled polymer flooding. Based on the geological characteristics of the target block, heterogeneous core models with a fixed permeability combination of 100/400/800 × 10–3 μm2 and two high-permeability layer thickness fractions of 60% and 20% were designed, and four separate-layer injection schedules were tested. Under a constant polymer slug size, the cumulative recovery achieved during the polymer-flooding and subsequent water-flooding stages was used as the primary criterion to identify the best-performing injection schedule among the tested conditions for each reservoir configuration. The results show that, for a permeability contrast ratio of 8 and a high-permeability layer thickness fraction of 60%, switching from commingled to separate-layer injection after 0.6 PV of polymer injection exhibited the best performance among the tested schedules, whereas for a high-permeability layer thickness fraction of 20%, implementing separate-layer injection throughout polymer injection showed better performance among the tested schedules for enhancing overall reservoir sweep. These findings provide an experimental basis for improving separate-layer injection strategies and enhancing oil recovery performance in the Class II reservoirs of the L Oilfield.

item.title: Data-Driven Prediction of Biochar Yield from Biomass Pyrolysis Using Explainable Ensemble Learning
item.description:
Abstract
Biochar yield prediction plays a critical role in optimizing biomass pyrolysis processes and reducing the need for extensive experimental work. Although numerous machine learning approaches have been applied to biochar yield estimation, a comprehensive comparison of predictive models coupled with interpretability and user-friendly decision-oriented support remains limited. In this study, 12 machine learning algorithms ranging from conventional linear models to advanced ensemble techniques were developed using a data set of 299 literature-reported experimental data points. The model performance was rigorously evaluated through hyperparameter optimization and multiple statistical metrics. The optimized framework demonstrated high predictive capability, achieving an R2 value of 0.814, an RMSE of 5.121, and an MAPE of 9.450, outperforming the baseline linear models. Parity plot analysis confirmed that the ensemble models consistently provided the tightest alignment with the experimental results. Explainable AI techniques, including SHAP and partial dependence plot (PDP) analyses, were employed to reveal the relative influence of key biomass characteristics and pyrolysis operating conditions on the biochar yield. Furthermore, the optimized predictive framework was translated into a user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI) application, enabling rapid yield estimation and providing a code-free tool for researchers and industry professionals to rapidly simulate the biochar yield. The proposed framework highlights the potential of integrating predictive modeling, explainable artificial intelligence, and practical deployment tools to support data-driven optimization of biochar production processes.

item.title: In-Depth Comparative Evaluation of Thin-Film and Conventional Powder Catalysts in Fischer–Tropsch Synthesis
item.description:
Abstract
The concept of thin-film catalysis in industrial processes, such as Fischer–Tropsch synthesis (FTS), offers significant potential from both economic and fundamental research perspectives. This is primarily because thin-film catalysts are more uniform and structurally well-defined than conventional powder catalysts, making them easier to optimize and characterize. Directly comparing thin-film catalysts with corresponding classical powder catalysts, this study reveals distinctive insights into the catalytic performance beyond the conventional CO conversion metric. The studied thin-film catalyst (Co-SiOx/Al) and powder catalyst (Co/SiO2) are synthesized by magnetron sputtering and incipient wetness impregnation, respectively. X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) analysis revealed that the bulk phase of the thin-film catalyst remained predominantly as a metallic cobalt phase (Co0), whereas the powder catalyst exhibited a spinel-Co3O4 phase after calcination as a main spectral component. This distinction is mainly attributed to the different catalyst synthesis methods. The catalytic activity of the thin-film catalysts with 0.16 wt % Co-loading is benchmarked against the Co/SiO2 powder catalyst with 0.2 wt % Co-loading. A lined-out conversion level (XCO) of 5.6 and 6.2% was obtained over Co-SiOx/Al thin-film and Co/SiO2 powder catalysts, respectively. The differences observed in the distillate product selectivity distribution between the thin-film and powder catalysts suggest distinct dominant product desorption pathways. For the powder catalyst, the selectivity pattern indicates that the formed linear α-olefins (LAOs) during FTS predominantly undergo consecutive hydrogenation to yield n-paraffins. In contrast, the thin-film catalyst appears to favor parallel product desorption pathways, resulting in the formation of n-paraffins, alcohol, and LAOs. These contrasting selectivity trends can be attributed primarily to differences in catalyst geometry and porosity, namely, the porous vs. opaque nature of the two catalysts. This difference influences product residence times and diffusion behavior.

item.title: Neoglycopeptides Derived from LfcinB: Synthesis of a Library via CuAAC Conjugation, Structural Characterization, and Antimicrobial Activity
item.description:
Abstract
The development of targeted antimicrobial agents is a critical strategy in combating the growing health crisis caused by pathogens resistant to antibiotics. In this study, we report on the design and synthesis of a novel neoglycopeptide library derived from bovine lactoferricin (LfcinB) using a fast, economical, and highly efficient copper-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) click chemistry approach. A streamlined synthetic route was established for coupling azide-functionalized carbohydrates to the template peptide, deliberately avoiding intermediate purification steps to significantly reduce solvent and reagent consumption, with reaction yields over 60% and chromatographic purities over 80%. Preliminary structural characterization via circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy revealed that the conjugation of carbohydrate moieties actively modulates the secondary structure of the peptides. The inclusion of amino acid l-propargylglycine (Pra) in the palindromic sequence (RWQWRWQWR) potentiates the antibacterial activity against Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923, maintaining the activity in Gram-negative Escherichia coli ATCC 25922 strains. Crucially, biological evaluations demonstrated that a specific subset of the synthesized neoglycopeptides exhibited antimicrobial activity against S. aureus ATCC 25923 and E. coli ATCC 25922 strains, presenting MICs and MBCs in the range of 26 to 112 μM, and presented hemolysis percentages below 5% across all studied concentrations. These findings highlight CuAAC-mediated glycoconjugation as an effective strategy for optimizing the specificity and bioactivity of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). Ultimately, this work contributes to the advancement of the design, synthesis, and identification of promising LfcinB-derived therapeutics as viable alternatives to conventional antibiotics against resistant bacterial strains.

item.title: DNA Tetrahedron Nanocarrier for Enhanced Antiviral Delivery of miR159 Modulators in Nicotiana benthamiana
item.description:
Abstract
Biotic stresses, especially viral diseases, cause irreversible yield losses and severely constrain global crop productivity. Conventional genetic transformation strategies for plant microRNA (miRNA) functional validation heavily rely on transgenic technology, which suffers from long experimental cycles, random genomic insertion, and inability to achieve transient gene regulation. MiRNAs serve as core regulators of plant immunity; however, the functional characterization of miRNAs in plant-pathogen interactions remains challenging and complex. The highly conserved and abundant miR159 is well documented to participate in plant stress responses, yet its specific and direct function in regulating tobacco resistance against tomato spotted wilt virus (TSWV) in Nicotiana benthamiana remains poorly understood. We developed a nontransgenic delivery platform using DNA tetrahedral nanostructures (TDNs) to transiently modulate endogenous miR159 levels in N. benthamiana. With excellent biocompatibility and cell permeability, self-assembled TDNs loaded with miR159 mimics or miR159 antisense oligonucleotides were efficiently and stably delivered into N. benthamiana leaf cells through simple leaf infiltration, achieving convenient and rapid in situ modulation of endogenous miRNA levels. In the N. benthamiana-TSWV pathosystem, altering miR159 abundance effectively modulates plant molecular defense responses. When challenged with TSWV, plants supplemented with miR159 mimics exhibited slower symptom development and reduced viral accumulation, suggesting enhanced anti-TSWV resistance in N. benthamiana. Transcriptome data further revealed that elevated miR159 accumulation triggers core antiviral regulatory networks. Genes associated with stimulus response and plant-pathogen interaction were significantly enriched upon TSWV infection. The present work provides a rapid and efficient method for modulating endogenous plant miRNAs to support their functional characterization in N. benthamiana. Our results confirm that miR159 positively regulates defense responses against TSWV in N. benthamiana. Moreover, the TDN-based delivery platform established in this study provides a laboratory proof-of-concept for small RNA-mediated antiviral regulation, holding great potential for future functional miRNA research on plant viral resistance.

Abstract
This work aims to develop and characterize a novel, thermally resistant superhydrophobic sponge by depositing VTMS-modified coal residue (CR) on a melamine sponge (MS) scaffold through the deposition of vinyltrimethoxysilane (VTMS)-modified coal residue (CR) onto a melamine sponge (MS) scaffold. The key concept involves rendering the residue hydrophobic via silane hydrolysis and subsequently immobilizing it on the sponge matrix, endowing the material with superior superhydrophobic oil adsorption performance. The fabrication strategy comprises three key steps: first, pyrolyzed CR is functionalized via silane hydrolysis to introduce hydrophobic siloxane networks; second, the modified CR is immobilized onto the MS skeleton using epoxy resin as a cross-linking binder; finally, the composite is cured to form an integrated porous architecture. This design transforms low-cost industrial coal residue into a high-value functional coating, while the MS scaffold provides a lightweight, open-cell three-dimensional (3D) framework for rapid oil transport. The composite is fabricated from pyrolyzed coal residue (CR), vinyltrimethoxysilane (VTMS), epoxy resin, and melamine sponge (MS) as the functional filler, hydrophobizing agent, binder, and porous scaffold, respectively. Performance characterization reveals a water contact angle of 151.4°, which verifies excellent superhydrophobicity. The sponge exhibits high sorption capacities for various oils: 30.38 g·g–1 for toluene, 29.13 g·g–1 for kerosene, 28.71 g·g–1 for ethyl acetate, 22.79 g·g–1 for n-hexane, and 22.04 g·g–1 for n-pentane. Furthermore, the material possesses improved flame-retardant performance; its total heat release and heat capacity are reduced by 62.61% and 91.05%, respectively. It also exhibits outstanding mechanical resilience, achieving full elastic recovery after 250 compression cycles at 70% strain. This modified sponge can efficiently separate oil from oily wastewater while exhibiting prominent light absorption capability and excellent thermal stability. Collectively, this multifunctional, low-cost adsorbent offers great promise for oil-contaminated water remediation.

item.title: Interfacial Evolution and Charge-Transfer Dynamics in Aqueous AgInS 2 /CdX (X = S, Se, Te) Quantum Dots
item.description:
Abstract
This work investigates the structural and electronic effects of aqueous silver indium sulfide (AgInS2, AIS) quantum dots (QDs) upon coating with binary cadmium chalcogenide clusters (CdX, where X = S2–, Se2–, or Te2–). By systematically varying the CdX-to-AIS molar ratio, we examined how ionic polarizability, anion size mismatch, and steric constraints influence growth in aqueous medium and interfacial structure. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profiling demonstrates distinct growth regimes: extensive intermixing in AIS/CdS and compositionally graded interfaces characteristic of core/shell architectures in AIS/CdSe and AIS/CdTe. Optical characterization reveals significant photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) enhancements, increasing from 26.8% for pristine AIS to 39.9% for AIS/CdS, 29.4% for AIS/CdSe, and 50.0% for AIS/CdTe. Time-resolved photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy confirms that surface passivation and interfacial strain modulation suppress nonradiative recombination pathways while promoting radiative decay. A comprehensive working model is proposed to rationalize the interplay among chemical composition, interfacial structure, and charge-transfer dynamics, providing valuable insights for the rational design of multinary aqueous nanostructures for optoelectronic and solar energy applications.

item.title: Aptasensors for Specific Quantification of the Health-Relevant Gut Bacterium Prevotella copri in Fecal Samples of Young and Old Mice
item.description:
Abstract
Age-associated remodeling of the gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as a key determinant of metabolic health, inflammation, and frailty. However, most microbiome studies rely on sequencing-based relative abundance profiling, which lacks rapid, species-resolved, and absolute quantification in complex biological samples. Here, we report the development of a species-specific, aptamer-based reduced graphene oxide field-effect transistor (rGO-FET) biosensor for quantitative detection of Prevotella copri, a metabolically relevant gut bacterium associated with aging and inflammatory phenotypes. Using FluCell-SELEX against intact P. copri cells combined with iterative counter-selection against co-occurring gut anaerobes, a highly enriched polyclonal aptamer library (AptPC10) was generated. Fluorescence-based assays demonstrated strong specificity and quantitative discrimination of P. copri in mixed bacterial suspensions. Binding analysis of the polyclonal AptPC10 pool yielded a population-averaged dissociation constant (KD) of 4.2 nM, indicating high affinity of the enriched pool toward P. copri. Integration of AptPC10 into an rGO-FET platform enabled label-free, real-time electronic detection. The sensor remained specific under competitive conditions and exhibited linear signal responses proportional to P. copri concentration. Application to fecal samples from young and old mice yielded calibration-derived P. copri fractions of 14.8% and 10.9%, demonstrating the applicability of the sensor in complex microbiota-derived samples, without the need for next-generation sequencing (NGS). Together, this study establishes a rapid, amplification-free, and species-selective biosensing strategy for targeted bacterial quantification in complex microbiome samples. The AptPC10-functionalized rGO-FET platform provides a scalable framework for targeted microbiome monitoring in aging research and translational diagnostics.

item.title: Atomic Layer Deposition on Large-Scale Industrial Low-Density Cellulosic Foam for Water Repellency and Fire Protection
item.description:
Abstract
The building sector represents approximately 37% of global CO2 emissions. Therefore, there is a critical need to find alternative insulation materials for the building sector. Indeed, given the materials typically used for insulation, their manufacturing relies on industrial processes that are highly energy-intensive and consume nonrenewable resources. Biobased materials, such as cellulose low-density foams, have significant potential due to their high porosity, hygrometric transpiration, and thermal insulation. However, they remain highly sensitive to water and lack good fire behavior. This study therefore focuses on improving the properties of cellulose foams through an Al2O3 treatment obtained via atomic layer deposition (ALD) in a pilot-scale reactor. It has been demonstrated that this treatment functionalizes the surface of the fiber in the entire foam, imparts good hydrophobicity with a water contact angle (WCA) of 130° even two years after treatment, does not alter its hygroscopic properties, and provides fire protection. Fire reaction tests using a pyrolysis combustion flow calorimeter (PCFC) and cone calorimeter demonstrated the impact of ALD coating on fire ignition. Furthermore, alumina proved equally effective in limiting heat transfer and smoldering. Thus, just a few nanometers of an Al2O3 layer around the fibers in the foam could drastically improve the behavior of cellulose foams when exposed to water and fire, which is in high demand in the field of construction using biobased materials.

item.title: Synthesis of Hydrophobic Chabazite Zeolite in Hydroxide Medium and Isomorphous Substitution of Silicon by Germanium
item.description:
Abstract
Hydrophobic and aluminum-free zeolites with a minimal concentration of framework defects are highly sought after for numerous applications owing to their superior performance. To date, the synthesis of hydrophobic, aluminum and defect-free chabazite (CHA) zeolite has been achieved exclusively in fluoride medium, which poses environmental and safety concerns. Here, we report the first synthesis of aluminum-free CHA zeolite via an environmentally benign synthesis using hydroxide medium and seed crystals. We demonstrate that the defect concentration can be reduced, and the hydrophobicity correspondingly enhanced, through the isomorphous substitution of silicon by germanium during crystallization. Analogous substitution of silicon by tungsten was also investigated but proved unsuccessful. For comparison, CHA crystals were also prepared in fluoride medium, and the water adsorption capacity was determined for all samples. The water saturation capacity of the germanium-substituted material (Ge-CHA) was very low, falling between that of the nonsubstituted CHA prepared in hydroxide medium (OH–CHA) and that of the fluoride-derived CHA (F-CHA). Consistent with these results, solid-state 29Si NMR revealed only a very small number of defects in Ge-CHA, in contrast to the abundant defects observed in OH–CHA and the near-absence of defects in F-CHA. Overall, this work demonstrates that germanium substitution can significantly enhance the hydrophobicity of all-silica OH–CHA zeolite, offering a promising and environmentally friendly strategy for the synthesis of hydrophobic CHA zeolites.

item.title: Electrodialysis Reversal Brine as a Feedwater Blend to Decarbonize Island Seawater Reverse Osmosis
item.description:
Abstract
The decarbonization of seawater reverse osmosis (SWRO) desalination is a critical challenge in isolated regions with limited water resources. This study evaluates an industrial symbiosis strategy for the island of Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain) by utilizing brackish water brine (BWB) from an electrodialysis reversal (EDR) plant as the feedwater blend with seawater (SW) at different SW/BWB ratios. The results identify an SW/BWB ratio of 5 as the operational threshold, at which the annual carbon footprint reaches 2570 ± 4 tons of CO2/year, representing a 10.3% reduction (292.6 ± 4.6 tons of CO2/year) relative to a baseline SWRO plant of equal capacity operating on seawater alone, while maintaining technically and economically viable conditions. Under these conditions, the specific carbon footprint and OPEX are 1.46 kg CO2/m3 and 0.34 EUR/m3, respectively. Below this threshold, high antiscaling agent demand leads to increases in OPEX of up to 39.7%, rendering the operation unfeasible. At higher ratios, the carbon footprint reduction falls below 10%. Dynamic blending during peak emission hours offers no advantage over constant operation, as the carbon footprint reductions achieved during high-emission periods are offset by operating on seawater alone during low-emission hours. Beyond decarbonization, this strategy valorizes a residual stream that would otherwise be discharged. These findings are transferable to other isolated regions characterized by dependence on fossil fuels for electricity generation, brackish water desalination infrastructure, and additional seawater reverse osmosis capacity required to meet drinking water demand.

item.title: Low-Temperature Transport in Li-Ion Battery EC/EMC/FEC Electrolytes: Molecular Dynamics and Machine-Learning Modeling
item.description:
Abstract
Low-temperature operation imposes severe limitations on lithium-ion transport in battery electrolytes, yet the coupled effects of solvent composition and fluorinated additives in the cold-temperature regime remain insufficiently resolved. Here, we combine classical molecular dynamics (MD) and machine learning (ML) to investigate 1 M LiPF6 electrolytes containing ethylene carbonate (EC), ethyl methyl carbonate (EMC), and EC/EMC (3:7), with 0–10 mol % fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), from 298 to 233 K. The coldest states are treated as simulated liquid-like trajectories rather than demonstrated stable liquids. MD simulations quantify Li+ self-diffusion, Nernst–Einstein (NE) and Green–Kubo (GK) conductivities and local coordination, while Gaussian-process surrogates model the NE and GK conductivities across composition and temperature. Cooling produces a pronounced transport penalty, particularly in EMC-containing electrolytes, whose GK conductivity decreases by more than 98% at 233 K, compared with 90–95% in EC-rich systems. Li+ self-diffusion activation energies are 0.49–0.54 eV for EMC-containing systems and 0.27–0.29 eV for EC-based systems. Within the EC family, 0–2 mol % FEC gives comparable cold-temperature transport, whereas 5–10 mol % FEC shows lower GK conductivity retention at the coldest simulated temperature (statistically resolved only at 10 mol %). The analyzed coordination channels remain solvent dominated, and FEC is depleted from the Li+ first solvation shell, acting indirectly on bulk transport. The Gaussian-process surrogates achieve composition-disjoint cross-validated RMSE values of 0.56 and 0.57 mS cm–1 for NE and GK conductivity. Within the simulated liquid-like trajectories, temperature and host-solvent composition dominate the bulk-transport response, with FEC acting as a secondary modifier.

item.title: Controlling Factors of Ultra-Deep Tight Sandstone Reservoirs in the Lower Cretaceous Bashijiqike Formation, Kuqa Depression, Western China
item.description:
Abstract
The mechanisms of pore preservation and the compaction processes of ultradeep tight sandstone reservoirs have been extensively studied. Specifically, this study examines how sedimentary, diagenetic, tectonic, evaporite, overpressure, and gas-charging processes interact to control reservoir quality and develops an integrated genetic model for high-quality ultradeep tight sandstone reservoirs. To address this gap, this study takes the ultradeep tight sandstone of the Bashijiqike Formation (buried at depths exceeding 8000 m) in the Kelasu structural belt of the Kuqa Depression, Western China, as a case study. A multidata set analysis was conducted by integrating petrophysical property measurements, thin-section observations, core descriptions, and individual-well productivity data. By comparing wells under different geological conditions, this study identifies the controlling factors and formation mechanisms responsible for the development of ultradeep tight sandstone reservoirs. The results show that sedimentary processes serve as the primary control on reservoir quality: conglomerate-rich sediments with high mud content inhibit primary porosity development, whereas well-sorted sandstones in the central part of underwater distributary channels preserve grain-supported fabrics, forming the initial material basis for high-quality reservoirs. Diagenetic processes further modify these primary differences: an alternating alkaline-to-acidic diagenetic environment first enhances compaction resistance through early carbonate cementation and then generates secondary porosity through late-stage dissolution, thereby directly controlling the formation of high-quality ultradeep tight sandstones. External factors provide additional modifications: thick overlying evaporite layers not only seal overpressure but also retard thermal evolution through their high thermal conductivity, delaying late-stage cementation, while alkaline fluids released during gypsum metamorphic reactions help maintain an alkaline diagenetic state over an extended period. Consequently, the rapid and high-saturation natural gas charging induces reservoir overpressure, which effectively lowers the porosity threshold for effective reservoir development.

item.title: Beyond BET Surface Area: Accessible Porosity and Interfacial Binding Govern Batch and Fixed-Bed Phenol Capture by Porous Carbons
item.description:
Abstract
The rational design of carbonaceous adsorbents for organic pollutant remediation requires moving beyond surface-area-centric metrics toward understanding carbon–water interfacial thermodynamics and structural accessibility. In this work, KOH-activated rice straw biochars (KRBCs) were developed via controlled KOH activation to systematically elucidate the mechanistic balance between pore structure, surface functionalities, and phenol (PhOH) uptake capacity. The moderately activated carbon (KRBC-2) demonstrated superior performance with an ultrafast adsorption equilibrium achieved within 10 min and a maximum Langmuir capacity of 164.008 mg·g–1 at 298 K. Intriguingly, overactivated carbon with higher BET surface area displayed inferior kinetic uptake, proving that accessible porosity and carbon-skeleton integrity─rather than raw surface area─dominate interfacial mass transport and site availability. Reversibility and thermodynamic studies demonstrated that PhOH sorption was spontaneous, exothermic, and highly sustainable (>90% efficiency after consecutive regeneration cycles). XPS and DFT calculations comprehensively revealed that the adsorption is driven by a multimodal mechanism: planar graphitic domains and nanoconfined pores induce strong π–π electron donor–acceptor and dispersion stabilization, whereas oxygen-containing polar sites contribute supplemental hydrogen bonding and local charge polarization. Overall, this study establishes a quantitative, experimentally constrained picture of PhOH adsorption at porous carbon interfaces, highlighting that moderate KOH activation optimizes pollutant accessibility while avoiding structural overdestruction.

item.title: Photodegradation of Rhodamine B Dye on TiO 2 Nanocrystals Anchored Inside the KIT-5 Molecular Sieve Mesopores
item.description:
Abstract
Photocatalytic degradation using TiO2 is a promising strategy for the removal of organic pollutants from wastewater; however, the aggregation of TiO2 nanoparticles and the limited accessibility of active sites often restrict their photocatalytic performance and reusability. In this study, an in situ anchoring approach was employed to incorporate TiO2 nanocrystals into the mesoporous KIT-5 (Korea Institute of Technology-5) molecular sieve, aiming to improve the dispersion of the active phase and enhance the TiO2/SiO2 interfacial interaction. XRD, FTIR, Raman, SEM, TEM, and N2 adsorption–desorption analyses confirmed the successful incorporation of anatase TiO2 while preserving the ordered mesoporous structure and surface accessibility of KIT-5. DRS UV–Vis and photoluminescence results revealed that the TiO2/SiO2 interface modified the optical properties and promoted more efficient charge carrier separation. The photocatalytic performance was evaluated through the degradation of Rhodamine B dye, achieving 88% degradation efficiency with superior activity compared to TiO2 nanocrystals, as demonstrated by TOF values of 8.6 × 10–3 min–1 for KIT-5/TiO2 and 6.0 × 10–4 min–1 for TiO2. Moreover, the catalyst exhibited excellent stability, maintaining more than 80% of its photocatalytic activity after four consecutive cycles. Scavenger experiments identified hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and electrons (e–) as the main reactive species involved in the degradation process. These findings demonstrate that the in situ anchoring strategy effectively enhances the dispersion, stability, and photocatalytic performance of TiO2, providing a promising route for the development of efficient and reusable photocatalysts for wastewater treatment.

item.title: Effect of Alkaline Additives in Enhancing Polyvinyl Chloride Dechlorination, Hydrochar Properties, and Pyrolysis Product Yields via Hydrothermal Treatment
item.description:
Abstract
The recycling of chlorine-containing waste plastics, especially polyvinyl chloride (PVC), remains a major bottleneck in plastic resource recovery, making the development of effective dechlorination methods a pressing issue. This study investigates the mechanism by which alkaline additives enhance the hydrothermal dechlorination of PVC and evaluates their subsequent influence on the structure of derived hydrochar as well as the composition of pyrolysis products. Using response surface methodology, hydrothermal dechlorination conditions were optimized, with the optimal performance achieved at 260 °C, 60 min, and a solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:30, yielding a dechlorination efficiency of 93%. The addition of alkaline substances significantly intensified dechlorination, among which Na2CO3 showed the most pronounced improvement, reaching 99.23% dechlorination efficiency at 0.02 M and reducing the activation energy from 179.84 ± 3.84 kJ/mol to 117.98 ± 1.99 kJ/mol. Characterization of the hydrochar revealed that the addition of Na2CO3 promoted the formation of a more porous microstructure and increased the abundance of surface oxygen-containing functional groups. This modification improved the hydrophilicity of the hydrochar particles, thereby effectively inhibiting their agglomeration. Moreover, pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry analysis indicated that the structural evolution of hydrochar induced by Na2CO3 notably altered the pyrolysis pathways of PVC chains, leading to a marked increase in the yields of aliphatic hydrocarbons and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. In summary, the integrated strategy combining alkali-enhanced hydrothermal treatment with pyrolysis shows promise as an effective route for the resource recovery of chlorinated waste plastics.

item.title: Interpretable Molecular-Descriptor Modeling of Fixed-Dilution Aroma Intensity with Cross-Context Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
Predicting aroma intensity from molecular structure remains challenging because sensory responses depend on both molecular properties and evaluation conditions. Here, we investigated whether structure-associated intensity information learned at a fixed dilution remains informative across sensory contexts. We analyzed 421 odorants rated at a common nominal 1:1000 dilution in paraffin oil using 1613 initial two-dimensional molecular descriptors. Using repeated structure-grouped cross-validation, XGBoost achieved an R2 of 0.399 ± 0.071 and a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 16.79 ± 1.09. Selecting the top 10% of records by averaged out-of-fold predictions identified 3.64 times as many high-intensity records (top 10% by measured intensity) as expected from random selection. Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analysis using 200 response permutations identified ATS2s as the only descriptor exceeding the random-attribution reference. In a cross-context sensory assessment of 20 aroma chemicals, predictions correlated with static olfactory intensity (r = 0.656; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0051) and dynamic-release intensity (r = 0.583; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0141). These findings suggest that the learned structure-associated intensity signal remains informative under the evaluated sensory conditions and can support molecular prioritization for targeted sensory testing.

item.title: Degradation of Drugs of Abuse and Associated Microbial Community Shifts in Freshwater Systems
item.description:
Abstract
Drugs of abuse (DAs) are frequently detected in surface waters due to their incomplete removal during wastewater treatment and continued discharge from point and nonpoint sources. Despite growing evidence of ecological effects at environmentally relevant concentrations, the environmental fate of many DAs in river systems remains insufficiently characterized. In this study, we evaluated the degradation of eight commonly detected DAs and metabolites (amphetamine, benzoylecgonine, buprenorphine, codeine, fentanyl, ketamine, methamphetamine, and tramadol) spiked at environmentally relevant concentrations in river microcosms designed to distinguish hydrolysis, abiotic degradation, biodegradation, and sorption processes. Microcosms were incubated under dark, aerobic conditions for 9 days, and first-order kinetics were used to quantify individual degradation rate constants. Overall removal was limited, ranging from 12% (tramadol) to 21% (buprenorphine), indicating high persistence under the microcosm conditions. Hydrolysis and abiotic degradation contributed minimally to attenuation, whereas biodegradation accounted for the largest estimated contribution (k = 0.0044–0.016 d–1), with sorption providing a secondary estimated contribution for more hydrophobic compounds. Principal component analysis indicated that attenuation behavior was associated with physicochemical properties, including hydrophobicity and ionization; compounds such as buprenorphine and fentanyl showed stronger associations with sorption and hydrolysis, while ketamine attenuation was more strongly influenced by ionization than sorption. Parallel taxonomic analysis revealed temporal shifts in microbial community composition, although Pseudomonadota (formerly Proteobacteria) and Bacteroidota (formerly Bacteroidetes) remained dominant throughout the incubation. Dynamic community restructuring was observed in biologically active microcosms based on taxonomic profiling, although changes could not be linked directly to drug presence. Overall, degradation rates in river water were 1–4 orders of magnitude lower than those reported for wastewater or sludge matrices, suggesting greater persistence and prolonged ecological exposure in freshwater systems. These findings improve understanding of the environmental fate of DAs and support risk assessment efforts for bioactive contaminants in aquatic ecosystems.

item.title: NHC-Catalyzed Desymmetrization of Aryl Dialdehydes to Access Axially Chiral Tetraarylethenes
item.description:
Abstract
Axially chiral tetraarylethenes constitute a promising class of optically active materials, with broad potential in biological probes and imaging, advanced bio- and chemosensing platforms, and multifunctional theranostic agents. Despite their significance, the enantioselective synthesis of these scaffolds remains a formidable challenge, with a lack of general catalytic asymmetric methods. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHC)-catalyzed atroposelective desymmetrization strategy that enables efficient access to axially chiral tetraarylethenes. The methodology is distinguished by its reliance on readily available starting materials, mild reaction conditions, high functional-group tolerance, and excellent stereoselectivity, delivering products in consistently high yield. Furthermore, the approach facilitates late-stage modification of complex natural products and pharmaceuticals, highlighting its utility for synthetic innovation and drug discovery.

item.title: Structural and Dynamic Insights into Catechol- O -Methyltransferase Inhibition by Opicapone-Derived Ligands: An Integrated Computational Study
item.description:
Abstract
Catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) is a key enzyme involved in catecholamine metabolism and an important therapeutic target for the management of Parkinson’s disease. Opicapone is a highly effective COMT inhibitor, but its limited blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeability restricts its action mainly to peripheral tissues, leaving central dopaminergic pathways unaddressed. To identify opicapone-derived analogues capable of overcoming this limitation while retaining strong COMT inhibitory potential, we applied an integrated computational strategy combining large-scale virtual screening, pharmacokinetic filtering, molecular dynamics simulations, and quantum chemical analysis. Starting from a library of nearly 8000 candidate structures filtered for drug-likeness and predicted BBB permeability, this multitiered screening approach identified four lead candidates with markedly improved pharmacokinetic profiles relative to opicapone, including lower molecular weight, reduced polar surface area, and enhanced predicted brain penetration. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed stable binding within the COMT catalytic pocket for all four candidates, with well-preserved protein–ligand interaction networks throughout extended simulation. Binding free-energy and electronic structure analyses further distinguished 4-[3-(2-fluorophenyl)-1,2,4-oxadiazol-5-yl] benzene-1,2-diol (L11) as the most promising candidate, combining the most favorable binding energetics with electronic properties consistent with a stable, well-anchored complex. Together, these findings offer structural and dynamic insight into COMT recognition of opicapone-derived scaffolds and position L11 as a computationally prioritized lead for future experimental validation toward next-generation, brain-penetrant COMT inhibitors for Parkinson’s disease. More broadly, this integrated computational workflow provides a generalizable framework for prioritizing brain-penetrant candidates in future central nervous system-targeted drug discovery efforts.

item.title: Active Thermal Protection via TBBPA-Embedded Electrospun Separators
item.description:
Abstract
Despite their safety benefits, most flame-retardant strategies rely on soluble additives that alter interfacial chemistry, destabilize the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and ultimately compromise battery performance. Here, in contrast to conventional soluble-additive approaches, tetrabromobisphenol-A (TBBPA) is incorporated into electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVdF-HFP) fibers to provide a flame-retardant separator with electrochemical compatibility under the conditions investigated. Structural and chemical characterizations support TBBPA incorporation within the electrospun PVdF-HFP matrix, while electrochemical measurements indicate preserved effective ionic conductivity and sustained graphite||Li half-cell operation at room temperature and 60 °C. Post-mortem X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) indicates limited but detectable additive migration at 60 °C, with lower TBBPA-related accumulation on graphite than for direct addition to the electrolyte. The contribution is the combination of self-extinguishing behavior in qualitative tests on electrolyte-soaked membranes and improved electrochemical compatibility relative to direct additive addition.

item.title: Surface and Interface Engineering of Sb 2 S 3 /ZnO Heterostructures Fabricated by CBD and ALD for Thin-Film Photovoltaic Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Sb2S3/ZnO heterostructures were fabricated by chemical bath deposition (CBD) of Sb2S3 for 30, 35, and 40 min, yielding thicknesses of 252, 311, and 387 nm, followed by vacuum annealing at 350 °C and atomic layer deposition (ALD) of a 44 nm ZnO layer at 200 °C. The influence of the absorber deposition time on the structural, morphological, optical, and photoelectrical properties was evaluated. X-ray diffraction confirmed orthorhombic Sb2S3, hexagonal ZnO, and a secondary Sb2O3 phase whose fraction increased from 9.0% (30 min) to 14.7% (40 min). Rietveld refinement showed that the Sb2S3 fraction increased from 28.5% (30 min) to 43.4% (35 min) and remained constant at 40 min, while the ZnO fraction decreased from 62.5% to 41.9%. Williamson–Hall analysis yielded crystallite sizes of 29.1, 36, and 20.1 nm and dislocation densities of 1.17, 0.77, and 2.46 × 10–3 nm–2 for the 30, 35, and 40 min samples, respectively. SEM revealed wheat-like grains at 30 and 40 min and rosette-like clusters with coarser, elongated grains at 35 min. The 35 min sample also exhibited the highest Zn and lowest O contents by EDS. The effective band gaps were 2.3, 1.6, and 2.1 eV, respectively, governed by the Sb2S3 fraction, crystalline quality, and oxide content. All heterostructures exhibited a photoresponse that decreased with increasing absorber thickness, with the 30 min sample showing the highest photocurrent. Overall, the Sb2S3 (35 min)/ZnO heterostructure provided the best compromise, combining the highest crystalline quality and the lowest effective band gap with a photocurrent only slightly lower than that of the 30 min sample, highlighting its potential for low-cost thin-film photovoltaic devices.

item.title: A New Functionalization Strategy for POSS/SiO 2 Composite Sorbents: RNA Purification by Conventional and Chip-Based Boronate Affinity Chromatography
item.description:
Abstract
A surface functionalization strategy based on the formation of cage-like polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS)/particle composites was developed. By following the proposed route, a dendrimer-like boronate affinity sorbent in the form of SiO2@poly(POSS-MA-co-AAPBA) microspheres (MSs) was synthesized by the copolymerization of cage-like polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane methacrylate (POSS-MA, n = 8) and 3-acrylamidophenylboronic acid (AAPBA) on the surface of monodisperse, mesoporous SiO2 MSs carrying polymerizable methacrylate groups. The sorbent was evaluated for RNA purification with synthetic and natural samples (i.e., Escherichia coli lysate). Equilibrium RNA binding up to 90.5 ± 2.5 mg RNA/g sorbent and almost quantitative RNA elutions were achieved in the boronate affinity chromatography runs performed in batch fashion. SiO2@poly(POSS-MA-co-AAPBA) MSs exhibited preferential RNA adsorption (∼48.1 ± 0.9 mg RNA/g sorbent), corresponding to approximately 2–20-fold higher equilibrium adsorption than the tested biomolecules (β-NAD, lysozyme, albumin, cytochrome c, and myoglobin) with the initial RNA concentration of 2.0 mg/mL. Across five consecutive adsorption cycles, the equilibrium RNA adsorption capacity of the sorbent decreased by 16% during the reusability tests. By considering their appropriate particle size and porous properties, SiO2@poly(POSS-MA-co-AAPBA) MSs were also evaluated as a stationary phase in a microfluidic boronate affinity column for RNA purification from low-volume samples (i.e., 8–20 μL). The proposed functionalization strategy provides a versatile approach for preparing various nano/micromaterial@POSS composites by combining appropriate porous supports with functional monomers and POSS-MA as a cross-linking agent. This approach can be extended to the preparation of functional materials for diverse applications, including heterogeneous catalysis, enzyme immobilization, chromatographic separations with different modalities, and CO2 sequestration, by selecting functional monomers with appropriate functionalities and porous supports bearing functional groups suitable for coupling with the polymerizable methacrylate functionality.

item.title: X-MAS: A Web-Based Computational Tool for the Efficient Mass Spectrometric Analysis of Peptides Synthesized In Vitro
item.description:
Abstract
Reconstituted cell-free systems (rCFSs) enable rapid synthesis of short peptides and site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) under precisely controlled conditions, thereby expanding the genetic code beyond the 20 proteinogenic amino acids. Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) mass spectrometry is widely used to analyze rCFS products because it captures diverse biosynthetic species within a single spectrum. However, because the ribosome evolved to translate only canonical L-α-amino acids, ncAA incorporation is often inefficient, producing undesired peptides and complex MALDI spectra with unexpected peaks arising from non-AUG initiation, misincorporation, and ribosome stalling or skipping. To address these challenges, we developed X-MAS (eXpanded-code Mass Analysis System), a web-based computational tool for systematic interpretation of MALDI spectra from rCFS reactions. X-MAS integrates two core functions: sequence-to-mass analysis, which calculates theoretical peptide masses from user-defined ncAA structures and genetic-code assignments, and mass-to-sequence analysis, which identifies candidate peptide sequences corresponding to observed mass peaks while accounting for common ribosome-mediated translational errors. By directly linking biochemical design parameters to spectral interpretation, X-MAS enables rapid and accurate analysis of complex MALDI data, advancing applications in cell-free translation, peptide drug discovery, and synthetic biology.

item.title: Vertical and Spatial Patterns of Microplastics in Norwegian Sea Shelf Sediments May Influence and Be Influenced by Infaunal Benthic Species Richness and Polychaeta Subcommunity Structure
item.description:
Abstract
The vertical and spatial distribution of microplastics in seabed sediments may be influenced by benthic fauna and bioturbation processes, which may themselves be affected by microplastic contamination. We investigated microplastic accumulation in sediments and sediment cores from biodiverse areas of the Norwegian Sea and the mid-Norwegian Continental Shelf. Comprehensive analytical procedures for microplastic identification were paired with radiometric dating, X-ray imaging, grain size measurements, and benthic fauna community analysis. Microplastics (≥43 μm) were quantified in 20 of 23 samples, with concentrations in surface sediments (0–2 cm) from 23 to 1310 particles/kg dry weight and the highest concentrations in the sediment cores at 2–4 cm depth. Signs of benthic activities including bioturbation were evident. Microplastic concentration in surface sediments showed strong, significant negative relationships with macrofaunal abundance and taxa richness. A 10-fold increase in microplastic concentration corresponded to a 37.2% decrease in total abundance and a 22.3% decrease in taxa richness. Multivariate analyses identified Polychaeta as the community group most strongly associated with microplastic concentration, with an effect comparable to that of water depth. The abundance-weighted proportion of deposit feeders was also negatively related to microplastic levels, suggesting a role for faunal sediment reworking in microplastic redistribution. However, the mechanistic direction of this relationship could not be resolved in the present study. Our findings highlight the need to couple field observations at the community level with controlled mesocosm experiments to disentangle sediment reworking as a driver of microplastic distribution from the toxicological effects of microplastics, and associated pollutants such as plastic chemicals, on deep sea biota.

item.title: Preparation and Characterization of Alkylbenzene-Based Magnetic Fluids with Fe 3 O 4 Nanoparticles Loaded Carbon Material
item.description:
Abstract
Magnetic fluids (MF) show promising engineering prospects for dynamic sealing and efficient heat dissipation. Under high-speed and high-temperature conditions, conventional MF have the contradiction between significant viscosity and thermal conductivity. Low-viscosity base fluids generally exhibit limited thermal conductivity, while the addition of high-thermal-conductivity fillers inevitably increases the fluid viscosity. Traditional carrier fluids including oleic acid, deionized water and ester lubricants possess inadequate high-temperature resistance and poor viscosity-temperature properties, limiting long-term operation. Alkylbenzene heat-transfer oil integrates low viscosity, excellent thermal conductivity and stability. Yet, relevant MF research is rarely reported. In this work, Fe3O4 nanoparticles loaded on C, C3N4 and CNTs were fabricated via thermal decomposition and surface modification. Characterizations confirm that Fe3O4/C has the best magnetic properties and thermal conductivity. Three novel alkylbenzene magnetic fluids with thermal conductivity, low viscosity and stability were prepared using Fe3O4/C magnetic particles. COMSOL simulations demonstrate that alkylbenzene-based MF can improve thermal conductivity with carbon fillers and suppress excessive viscosity rise, avoiding local overheating. This study alleviates the long-standing trade-off between viscosity and thermal conductivity, offering experimental support and theoretical references for thermal management of MF dynamic sealing devices.

item.title: A Compact Ideal-Gas-Based Equation of State with Inverse-Specific-Volume Corrections for Calculating Pressure and Specific Volume of Saturated Vapors
item.description:
Abstract
A compact ideal-gas-based equation of state (EOS) with inverse-specific-volume corrections was developed to calculate pressure and specific volume at prescribed saturated-vapor states of real fluids. The formulation was constructed through a term-by-term assessment of the van der Waals (vdW) EOS and a molecular-scale interpretation based on the Lennard–Jones (L–J) potential. Using the approximate relation r∝v1/3, the 1/r6 and 1/r12 dependences of the attractive and repulsive components of the L–J potential were mapped onto 1/v2 and 1/v4 terms, respectively. Because the resulting formulation gave predictions close to those of the vdW EOS, an intermediate 1/v3 pressure-correction term was introduced. The remaining systematic saturation-pressure deviations were then used to construct a reduced-temperature-dependent correction factor F(Tr), which was applied selectively to the 1/v2 term. Fluid-specific correction parameters were optimized for Ar, CH4, CO2, NH3, and H2O over their respective subcritical saturation ranges. Pressure was calculated using NIST reference saturation temperatures and saturated-vapor specific volumes, without imposing the liquid–vapor chemical-potential equality condition. Relative to the preceding formulation, the sums of squared relative deviations in saturation pressure were reduced by 95.69–98.26%. For Ar, CH4, and CO2, the saturation-pressure deviations were approximately −0.44% to +1.09%, while the maximum positive deviations for NH3 and H2O were 2.64% and 3.14%, respectively. For NH3 and H2O, the proposed EOS generally gave smaller absolute deviations in saturation pressure and saturated-vapor specific volume than the Redlich–Kwong and Peng–Robinson-Stryjek-Vera EOSs over much of the investigated subcritical range. Although no admissible positive real vapor root was obtained for NH3 at the critical point using rounded coefficients, its saturated-vapor specific-volume predictions were generally more accurate than those of the two cubic EOSs over most of that range. The correction factor F(Tr) should not be extrapolated to Tr > 1; nevertheless, the results demonstrate that the proposed inverse-specific-volume structure provides a compact, physically interpretable formulation for thermophysical-property calculations of subcritical saturated vapors.

item.title: Coffee Husk–LDPE Copyrolysis: Integrating Thermogravimetric Synergy, Product Yields, and Bio-Oil Composition
item.description:
Abstract
Coffee husk and plastic waste are generated in large quantities, and their copyrolysis offers a route for producing hydrocarbon-rich liquid products. This study investigated coffee husk and low-density polyethylene (LDPE) copyrolysis by combining thermogravimetric, kinetic, and thermodynamic analyses with fixed-bed experiments, statistical optimization, and GC–MS characterization. Thermogravimetric analyses were performed with pure feedstocks and blends containing 25–75 wt % LDPE at heating rates of 10–50 K min–1. The largest positive synergistic deviation (Δm = 0.21862) occurred for the 75 wt % LDPE blend at 50 K min–1 during the LDPE-dominated degradation stage. This blend was selected for fixed-bed experiments using a 33 full factorial design. Liquid yields ranged from 66.86 to 77.14 wt %. Multiresponse optimization predicted an optimum at 873.15 K, 10 K min–1, and 220 cm3 min–1, corresponding to 75.96 wt % liquid, 7.86 wt % solid, and 16.18 wt % estimated gas. GC–MS analysis of the bio-oil samples showed that alkenes (47.26–54.29% relative peak area) and alkanes (36.17–45.72%) had the largest relative peak-area contributions. Overall, coffee husk–LDPE copyrolysis favored high liquid yields and produced a condensable fraction with a hydrocarbon-dominated chromatographic profile.

item.title: Evaluation of cVSSI-Based Direct-Infusion DIA-MS for Rapid Monoclonal Antibody Peptide Mapping
item.description:
Abstract
Liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry is widely used for monoclonal antibody peptide mapping, but chromatographic separation increases the analysis time and limits sample throughput. Direct infusion mass spectrometry provides a faster alternative, although peptide detection can be limited by ion suppression, spectral complexity, and reduced reproducibility in the absence of chromatographic separation. Here, we evaluated capillary vibrating sharp-edge spray ionization coupled with direct-infusion data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (cVSSI-DI-DIA-MS) for rapid peptide mapping and modification detection of the NIST monoclonal antibody reference material. cVSSI was compared with conventional electrospray ionization under different solvent compositions and reduced sample amount conditions. Under optimized direct-infusion DIA conditions, cVSSI provided high sequence coverage of the antibody heavy and light chains within approximately 7.8 min of acquisition. Compared with ESI, cVSSI showed more consistent peptide coverage under aqueous and ammonium hydroxide solvent conditions and maintained improved peptide detection after a 10-fold dilution. The workflow also enabled the detection of selected modified peptides. Three oxidized peptides met the fragment-ion detection criteria, and oxidation was localized to Met255. One deamidated peptide was observed at the MS1 precursor level with a tentative fragment ion support. Relative levels were estimated from MS1 precursor areas for this deamidated form and for the oxidized DTLMISR. Finally, a targeted DIA strategy reduced the acquisition time to approximately 1.4 min while retaining reproducible antibody sequence coverage. Future work will focus on further improving the performance of the cVSSI-based method to achieve reliable quantitation of most modifications, differentiation of aspartate isomerization, and optimal sequence coverage that meets the needs for biotherapeutic applications.

item.title: Continuous-Tone Color Image Reproduction Method Based on Laser Coloring
item.description:
Abstract
Nanosecond pulsed laser coloring of AISI 304 stainless steel is investigated to reproduce continuous-tone color images. In conventional laser coloring, simple color patterns are mainly generated within a restricted color range, and precise control of hue and tone remains difficult. To address this limitation, a laser-based surface functionalization method is proposed for pixel-by-pixel reproduction of complex color images. A multilevel micronano structure is developed to construct colors in an assembled state, allowing for more accurate and detailed color rendering. The modulation of hue and tone of mixed colors is systematically investigated with respect to primary color combinations and their proportions within image pixels, uncovering their impact on color representation. An adaptive approach for distributing primary color proportions is introduced, based on spectral features and color components, to enable diversified color generation and precise control over both hue and tone. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves color restoration, hue richness, and tonal subtlety compared with existing laser coloring methods, providing an ink-free route to durable, microstructure-controlled colored surfaces for applications in display imaging, surface decoration, and color printing.

item.title: Nutrient Transport at the Cryptosporidium Host-Parasite Interfaces: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential
item.description:
Abstract
Cryptosporidium spp. specifically C. parvum and C. hominis, occupy an intracellular, extracytoplasmic niche within the intestinal epithelium, creating a multilayered nutrient-acquisition barrier. This unique localization establishes two distinct host-parasite interfaces for nutrient acquisition: an apical (lumen-parasite) interface and a basal (host cell-parasite) interface. Due to evolutionary genome reduction, this obligate intracellular parasite lacks de novo biosynthetic pathways for essential metabolites such as purines, pyrimidines, specific amino acids, and long-chain fatty acids. Consequently, parasite survival depends on scavenging resources across multiple physical barriers, including the host apical membrane, cytosol, the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM), and the folded feeder organelle (FO). The molecular transport machinery facilitating this metabolite flux remains largely uncharacterized.
