This review examines whether transporter function and localization represent critical points in Cryptosporidium pathophysiology and viable therapeutic targets. We analyze genomic and biochemical data to map the parasite transporter repertoire and compare it with other apicomplexans to evaluate potential drug targeting strategies. We also discuss three proposed models for nutrient flux (parasite transporter export, recruitment of host solute carriers, and nonselective pore mechanisms) and present an experimental framework to distinguish between them while identifying future research priorities.

item.title: Through-the-Bottle Fingerprinting of Red Wine Using Near-IR Fluorescence Spectroscopy
item.description:
Abstract
A major unaddressed challenge for food science remains the accurate characterization of contents in sealed containers with a noninvasive method. This issue is particularly pressing in the wine industry, valued at billions of dollars globally, where product identity, brand reputation, and consumer trust are paramount. While many techniques exist for analyzing red wine externally, to date, performing accurate classification of the contents within unopened bottles remains elusive. Through-container spectroscopy has previously targeted the Raman signal of the contents, whereas here we extend noninvasive spectroscopy to samples such as red wine, whose strong fluorescence overwhelms any Raman features. Using only a single near-infrared optical excitation source operating at a wavelength of 785 nm, in combination with a bespoke geometry to circumvent the confounding signal of the glass, we demonstrate that through-bottle fluorescence spectra can distinguish among different red wines in their original intact bottles. Principal component analysis (PCA) of 20 red wines reveals clear separation and a strong varietal grouping. Leave-one-bottle-out cross-validation of spectra of six wines measured through six different bottles distinguishes the wine irrespective of its container with a 96% mean accuracy (range 92–100%), confirming that the measurement is independent of the bottle. This rapid, noninvasive technique offers a route to characterizing high-value liquids through their packaging, with potential applications across the food, beverage, and pharmaceutical sectors.

item.title: Impact of Fc N-Glycan Presence and Composition on the Physicochemical and Chemical Stability of Trastuzumab
item.description:
Abstract
Fc N-glycans are critical quality attributes of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies, as they influence not only effector functions but also structural stability. However, the contributions of their presence and glycoform composition to antibody stability, including thermal stability, aggregation, fragmentation, and site-specific chemical degradation, remain unclear. To clarify the role of Fc glycans in maintaining antibody stability, trastuzumab samples with distinct Fc glycoforms, including untreated antibody, glycan-enriched (G0F, G2F, and G2S2F) variants, deglycosylated forms generated by PNGase F treatment, and partially deglycosylated forms generated by Endo S treatment, were subjected to heat and light stress conditions to evaluate glycan-dependent differences in physicochemical and site-specific chemical stability. Glycan remodeling was verified using intact mass spectrometry. Analysis by nanoDSF showed that deglycosylation decreased Tm1, whereas the G2S2F-enriched sample exhibited a modest increase in Tm1, indicating that Fc glycan structure may affect the thermal stability of the Fc region. Mass photometry and intact mass spectrometry revealed stress-dependent fragmentation, including species presumed to be derived from light-chain release, with more pronounced degradation under light stress and a tendency toward increased multimer formation. Although fragmentation and, to a lesser extent, multimerization were observed under stress conditions, glycoform-dependent differences were not consistently reproduced across analytical methods. Comprehensive peptide mapping analysis was performed to assess stress-induced deamidation and oxidation across the antibody sequence. The most pronounced glycoform-dependent difference was enhanced deamidation at N289 under heat stress in deglycosylated samples, whereas oxidation progressed under light stress but did not show consistent or reproducible differences among glycoforms. Overall, this study demonstrates that the presence of Fc N-glycans and their glycoform composition influence selected aspects of trastuzumab stability under forced degradation conditions, particularly thermal stability and N289 deamidation, highlighting the importance of Fc glycans in maintaining antibody stability. The observed effects were more strongly associated with glycan presence or absence than with differences among intact glycoforms.

item.title: Data-Efficient Machine Learning-DFT Workflow for Rapid Prediction of Polyaromatic Reactivity on Bimetallic Surfaces
item.description:
Abstract
Density functional theory (DFT) simulations have become an essential tool for studying surface reactivity at the microscale, providing guidelines for experimentalists in the design of efficient catalyst compositions across a wide range of applications. However, DFT calculations are resource-intensive and can be prohibitively time-consuming, especially when large adsorbates must be sampled across heterogeneous surfaces with many nonequivalent adsorption sites. In this work, we propose a joint ML–DFT workflow to accelerate the prediction of polyaromatic reactivity on bimetallic surfaces using carefully selected descriptors computed on related molecular fragments. To establish a proof of concept for this strategy, we focused on the hydrogenation of anthraquinone (AQ) to anthrahydroquinone (H2AQ)─a key step in the industrial production of hydrogen peroxide─on Pd-based alloys (25 and 50 at. % alloying ratios). We show that a relatively small data set (<100 samples) is sufficient to build predictive models with high accuracy and strong robustness using tree-based regression methods. Notably, despite the flexibility of these ML algorithms and the broad diversity of surface atomic arrangements and adsorbate configurations represented in our training set, overfitting could be effectively limited through careful selection of multidimensional descriptor sets and appropriate model tuning. With training mean absolute errors (train-MAEs) on the order of ∼0.15 eV for predicting AQ and H2AQ adsorption energies, as well as the AQ-to-H2AQ hydrogenation reaction energies, our model is competitive with state-of-the-art ML approaches in heterogeneous catalysis, including machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), which for certain surface classes and adsorbate types often struggle to achieve train-MAEs below ∼0.10 eV. Although developed here for polycyclic aromatic compounds, we anticipate that this strategy could be extended to other large, chemically complex molecular systems, helping bridge computational screening with experimental validation in industrially relevant catalyst design.

item.title: Development and Experimental Validation of a Sectional Combustion Model for Corn Stover Pellets
item.description:
Abstract
To investigate the combustion characteristics of densified biomass fuels and provide a basis for grate-fired boiler optimization, corn stover pellets were selected as the research subject. Utilizing a temperature-differential gas analysis method in a fixed-bed experiment, the combustion process was divided into five distinct stages: drying, volatile release and combustion, mixed combustion, char combustion, and burnout. Based on these stages, a sectional combustion model was established by mapping the stage boundaries identified at different bed heights in a time–height coordinate system and further distinguishing the char reduction and char oxidation zones according to the O2 and CO characteristics. A dedicated experimental furnace was designed. The furnace structure was further optimized through efficiency testing and numerical simulation analysis. The numerical results indicated that modifying the rear-arch configuration─specifically reducing its height from 575.7 mm to 400 mm, extending its horizontal projection from 800.5 mm to 1526 mm, and increasing its coverage ratio from 34.06% to 76.29%─strengthened heat feedback near the fuel-feeding region and enhanced flue-gas recirculation and gas mixing. Industrial tests showed that the average CO concentration in the flue gas decreased by 180.10 mg/m3, and the excess air coefficient was reduced by 0.65, thereby lowering both flue-gas heat loss and incomplete combustion loss. After optimization, the fuel consumption normalized to a boiler output of 1 t/h decreased from 309.79 to 301.60 kg/h, while the average slag temperature decreased by 15.03 °C. Consequently, the average direct and indirect thermal efficiencies of the boiler increased by 6.58 and 6.83 percentage points, respectively. These results indicate that linking fuel-bed combustion characteristics with the stage-specific requirements for heat feedback and oxygen supply can provide a practical basis for the structural optimization of biomass grate-fired boilers.

item.title: Cardanol Methacrylate as a Biobased Self-Cross-Linker in Waterborne Acrylic Latexes: From Challenges in Emulsion Polymerization to Film Performance
item.description:
Abstract
Cardanol methacrylate (CARMA) is a biobased methacrylate with increasing interest in the coating industry. Not only more than 80% of the carbon is obtained from renewable sources, but it also allows the production of self-cross-linkable latexes via oxidative cross-linking. However, the use of this monomer in an environmentally friendly process such as emulsion polymerization is challenging, due to its high hydrophobicity. To overcome these limitations in this work, we evaluate different approaches, including high-shear methods and the use of cosolvents or β-cyclodextrin as a diffusion enhancer. Among all strategies, β-cyclodextrin proved to be the most effective method, enabling high monomer conversion and up to 99% CARMA incorporation when the initiator and surfactant concentrations are optimized. Films prepared from the resulting latexes exhibit high gel contents even without an added drying agent, which in some cases hinders the film formation process. Moreover, the use of a drying agent substantially increases the effective cross-linking density, leading to a pronounced reduction in water uptake. Overall, this work provides effective strategies to overcome the diffusion limitations of CARMA in emulsion polymerization.

item.title: Transient LiCl Transport through Angstrom-Scale Graphene Slits: A Molecular Dynamics Study
item.description:
Abstract
Concentration-gradient-driven transport of aqueous LiCl through idealized neutral graphene slits with geometric widths of 6.15–11.07 Å was investigated using classical molecular dynamics simulations. Four independent 20 ns trajectories were analyzed for each slit width. In the 6.15 and 7.38 Å slits, Li+ and Cl– occupancy and signed net reservoir transfer were strongly suppressed, whereas water crossed all five slits. Atom-identity-resolved directional event counting revealed substantial bidirectional recrossing around the central graphene plane. Nevertheless, a conservative complete-translocation analysis identified the largest observed adjacent increase in finite-time, gradient-directed net reservoir transfer between 7.38 and 8.61 Å for both Li+ and Cl–, while the subsequent adjacent increases over 8.61–11.07 Å were smaller. These observations indicate a finite-width crossover from strong ion exclusion to measurable transfer rather than a unique critical threshold or a strict transport plateau. Density distributions showed progressive ion access to the wider slits and ion-specific interfacial organization near graphene. The pore hydrogen-bond number density was lowest in the narrowest confined regions and generally increased as confinement was relaxed. Representative slit-entry free-energy profiles further identified distinct metastable positions for Li+ and Cl– near the pore plane. These results provide a molecular-level picture of confinement-controlled LiCl transport and the associated changes in interfacial organization and confined water structure.

item.title: Structural and Enzyme Kinetic Basis Underpinning the Activity of 4-Anilinoquinazoline-Based Fourth-Generation EGFR Inhibitors
item.description:
Abstract
Acquired resistance to epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) remains a major challenge in the treatment of EGFR mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The EGFR gatekeeper mutation T790M confers resistance to first-generation EGFR inhibitors that act through ATP competition by increasing the affinity of the kinase for ATP. Third-generation inhibitors partially overcome this limitation by forming a covalent bond with Cys797, thereby enhancing their ability to compete with ATP; however, the C797S mutation abolishes this covalent interaction and leads to renewed drug resistance. To overcome C797S-mediated resistance, a range of so-called fourth-generation inhibitors have been developed, some of which retain the classical 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold. In this study, we compared the potencies of two such candidate compounds, BDTX-1535 and WSD0922, together with first- and second-generation inhibitors that also share the 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold, in clinically relevant cell models harboring EGFR C797S with or without T790M mutation. By combining the experimentally determined structure of EGFR/BDTX-1535 complex, molecular docking models of WSD0922, and analysis of the effects of the C797S mutation on EGFR kinase kinetics, we sought to explore structural and enzymatic factors associated with differences in inhibitor potency. These findings provide comparative insight into the behavior of 4-anilinoquinazoline-based EGFR inhibitors and may help guide subsequent inhibitor optimization.

item.title: Temperature-Controlled Structural and Surface Modulation of Bi/BiO x Electrocatalysts for High-Rate CO 2 Electroreduction to Formate
item.description:
Abstract
Bismuth-based electrocatalysts are promising materials for the electrochemical reduction of CO2 to formate; however, their performance depends strongly on structural and surface properties. Herein, Bibased catalysts synthesized at 100, 120, and 150 °C were systematically investigated to elucidate the influence of synthesis temperature on their physicochemical characteristics and electrocatalytic behavior in an alkaline flow-cell reactor. Rietveld refinement revealed a temperature-dependent evolution of the bulk crystalline phases, with Bi2O2CO3 and Bi2O3 predominating in Bi-100 and Bi-120, whereas metallic Bi became the major phase in Bi-150. Raman and XPS analyses further confirmed the coexistence of metallic and oxidized Bi species, with oxidized species remaining prevalent at the catalyst surfaces. Among the investigated materials, Bi-120 exhibited the highest BET specific surface area (43.0 m2 g–1) and double-layer capacitance, together with the lowest charge-transfer resistance (36.3 Ω cm2). These properties were associated with its more favorable hierarchical morphology and superior electrocatalytic performance, reaching geometric current densities of −80, −115, and −155 mA cm–2 at −0.8, −1.0, and −1.2 V vs RHE, respectively, while maintaining formate Faradaic efficiencies of approximately 90–95%. The maximum formate production rate was 4.43 mmol m–2 s–1 at −1.2 V vs RHE. Formate and H2 were the only products detected under the investigated conditions. Stability tests revealed distinct behavior depending on the gas diffusion electrode architecture. With conventional carbon paper, the formate Faradaic efficiency decreased markedly after the first hour of operation, falling from approximately 80% to below 50% and remaining at this lower level throughout the 22 h test, consistently with electrode wetting and flooding. In contrast, a PTFE-supported Bi-120 electrode sustained operation for a total of 20 h at −150 mA cm–2, maintaining formate Faradaic efficiencies above 60%, although fluctuations in product selectivity were observed. These findings demonstrate that synthesis-temperature control provides an effective strategy to tailor the structural, textural, and surface properties of Bibased electrocatalysts, while highlighting the importance of GDE architecture and wettability management for sustained CO2 electroreduction.

item.title: Effects of Oxygen Transfer Rates on the Bioanode Potential in Long-Term-Operated Terracotta Microbial Fuel Cells
item.description:
Abstract
In a single-chamber microbial fuel cell with an air cathode, the substrate-converting anaerobic biofilm at the anode produces electrons and protons. Efficient transfer of both products to the cathode improves the electric circuit performance. Minimizing the transfer resistance through the electrolyte can increase the undesired oxygen transfer in the reverse direction. This study examines how controlling the availability of dissolved oxygen as a terminal electron acceptor influences the bioanode’s electrode potential in membrane-free cells with a scalable design using low-cost terracotta separators that also provide structural support. The oxygen mass transfer rate varied with the regulation of the oxygen concentration in the air-cathode chamber. The anodes rapidly lost their negative potential below a substrate concentration of 300 mg O2 L–1 chemical oxygen demand in the municipal wastewater and 21 vol.% O2 at the air-cathode. When the oxygen concentration in the air-cathode chamber was reduced to 10 vol.%, the current density increased significantly while the separator-facing anode potentials remained below −200 mV (SHE) at the maximum power point. Cells with thinner separators and lower transfer resistance produced higher power. The cathodes performed stably under O2-limited conditions. However, the NH4–N elimination rate decreased to only 0.82 g NH4–N d–1 m–2 (±0.63). All cells exhibited stable performance without maintenance for over 400 days.

item.title: Electronic Structure of Co-Phthalocyanine Metal–Organic Framework
item.description:
Abstract
Two-dimensional (2D) metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) composed of metal phthalocyanines (MPc; MPc-MOF) are predicted to possess electronic structures similar to those of Dirac materials, such as the Lieb lattice and the fes lattice. Therefore, in this study, we first investigated the energy band structure of CoPc-MOF using density functional theory (DFT). According to previous theoretical studies, if the lattice structure of CoPc-MOF is regarded as a Lieb lattice, its π-band is predicted to exhibit stronger Dirac-band-like characteristics compared to other MPc-MOFs containing metals. The electron density obtained from the energy band calculations indicated that the contribution of the central metal to the π-band of CoPc-MOF is small; therefore, the lattice structure can be assumed to be more similar to the fes lattice than to the Lieb lattice. Next, we evaluated the crystal structure of the synthesized CoPc-MOF using X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The TEM images revealed that the synthesized CoPc-MOF powder consists of flake-like microcrystals, in which crystal growth along the molecular layer stacking direction is minimal. Furthermore, the absorption spectra in the visible and near-infrared (Vis–NIR) regions indicate that CoPc-MOF is a narrow-gap semiconductor with an optical gap of approximately 0.36 eV. On the other hand, DFT calculations indicate that the CoPc-MOF crystal is metallic due to the formation of a π-band in the interlayer direction (along the c-axis), which is inconsistent with the experimental results. This suggests that the synthesized CoPc-MOF may not be sufficiently stacked in the interlayer direction. This finding is consistent with the TEM images, which show that CoPc-MOF consists of flake-like microcrystalline structures. Energy band calculations were performed on a single monolayer of CoPc-MOF; however, even a single monolayer of CoPc-MOF behaves as a metal when electronic correlations are not explicitly considered, which contradicts the Vis–NIR and UPS experimental results. The single molecular layer of CoPc-MOF exhibited a metallic ground state because the π-d bands near the Fermi level formed the Fermi surface. In conclusion, the DFT+U energy-band calculations for the CoPc-MOF monolayer reproduced a semiconducting ground state and best explained the UPS spectra. These results indicate that the electronic correlation effects are significant in the 2D π-d bands near the Fermi level of a single molecular layer of CoPc-MOF.

item.title: Interfacial Charge Redistribution and Orbital-Selective Fe–Ni Ferromagnetism in LaFeO 3 /LaNiO 3 Superlattices
item.description:
Abstract
Controlling exchange through interfacial charge and orbital reconstruction is a promising route to high-temperature magnetism in oxide superlattices. (LaNiO3)n/(LaFeO3)1 superlattices exhibit ferromagnetism up to 608 K, with the strongest response at n = 1. Here, spin-polarized density functional theory with Hubbard corrections, charge-density analysis, orbital-resolved electronic structure, magnetic-energy mapping and atomistic Monte Carlo simulations reveal the microscopic origin of this behavior. In the n = 1 period, interfacial charge redistribution produces a net Fe-to-Ni electron transfer of 0.0508e and a Ni moment of 1.609 μB, of which 1.559 μB resides in the eg manifold. Reversal of the Ni layer costs 519 meV per 1 × 1 period, and a seven-shell mapping of 19 magnetic configurations identifies a leading nearest-neighbor Fe–Ni exchange of +26.9 meV. Layer-resolved magnetic configurations for n = 3 and 5 further show that interfacial Ni moments are magnetically stiffer than inner-layer Ni moments. A DFT-calibrated Monte Carlo model yields a zero-strain ordering temperature of 525–530 K, close to the experimental value. Biaxial strain tunes Ni–O bonding, Ni polarization and the relative Fe–Ni and Ni–Ni magnetic energy scales. These results establish interfacial Ni eg polarization as the orbital route by which charge redistribution stabilizes Fe–Ni ferromagnetism in nickelate-ferrite superlattices and identify a materials-design route toward high-temperature oxide spintronic elements and ultrathin magnetic-storage architectures.

item.title: Molecular Interaction between Ovalbumin and Quercitrin: Binding Mechanism and Functional Enhancement
item.description:
Abstract
To elucidate the interaction mechanism between ovalbumin (OVA) and quercitrin (QUE) and its effects on the structural and functional properties of the resulting complex, an OVA-QUE system was constructed and characterized using spectroscopic techniques, differential scanning calorimetry, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. The results showed that QUE formed a complex with OVA and quenched its intrinsic fluorescence through a mechanism consistent with predominantly static quenching, with binding constants on the order of 104 L·mol–1 and approximately one binding site. Synchronous fluorescence, three-dimensional fluorescence, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy revealed that QUE binding altered the microenvironment surrounding the aromatic amino acid residues and induced local conformational changes in OVA, with a more pronounced effect on tryptophan residues. Molecular docking identified one plausible binding pocket composed of both polar and hydrophobic residues, in which QUE may interact with key residues through hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic contacts. Molecular dynamics simulations further indicated that the Mode 1 predicted OVA-QUE pose remained stably accommodated throughout the trajectory without disrupting the overall protein fold while reducing the local flexibility of binding-pocket residues. However, these simulations cannot distinguish the Mode 1 pose from other nearly isoenergetic docking sites. The functional analysis indicates that QUE binding raises the thermal transition temperature of the freeze-dried OVA-QUE complex from 120.5 to 132.6 °C, indicating a change in the thermal transition behavior of the freeze-dried complex in the solid state. Moreover, the binding of QUE also reduces protein aggregation near the isoelectric point and enhances the ability of QUE to scavenge DPPH and ABTS free radicals. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that OVA forms a relatively stable complex with QUE through hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic interactions and that this association alters the thermal transition behavior of the freeze-dried complex, improves dispersion behavior near the isoelectric point, and enhances antioxidant performance by modulating the local conformation of the protein. This study provides a theoretical basis for the development of functional ingredients based on protein–glycosylated flavonoid complexes and for further investigation of their structure–function relationships.

item.title: Upcycled Silicon-Rich Backgrinding Waste from the Semiconductor Industry into Catalytic-Magnetic Nanocomposites for Water Remediation
item.description:
Abstract
Wafer backgrinding process in the semiconductor industry generates large volumes of dilute backgrinding wastewater (DBGW), resulting in the loss of approximately 70% of high-purity silicon in the form of polydisperse nanosized silicon-rich colloids. The high zeta potential (−38.7 mV) of the Si colloids further confirmed their strong colloidal stability and highlights their potential for engineering valorization. In this work, silicon-rich waste recovered from semiconductor DBGW was directly upcycled as a functional support for the construction of Si-PDDA-IOMNPs nanocomposites through layer-by-layer surface functionalization with poly(diallyldimethylammonium) chloride (PDDA) and iron oxide magnetic nanoparticles (IOMNPs), resulting in an open shell core–shell architecture. The potential application of magnetically responsive particles in water treatment as adsorbents and heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysts holds great promise for effective degradation and removal of pollutants from aqueous environments. This potential dual adsorbent-catalyst role was further evaluated with the organic dye removal studies using Methylene Blue (MB) and Methyl Orange (MO) as model systems. The Si-PDDA-IOMNPs nanocomposite exhibited high removal efficiencies toward MB (100%) and MO (94.25%) in the presence of H2O2, demonstrating its potential for combined adsorption and oxidative dye removal. Sedimentation kinetics and Derjaguin–Landau–Verwey–Overbeek (DLVO) analysis further revealed that the nanocomposite possesses a substantial energy barrier (∼25.4 kBT), which suppresses aggregation and improves colloidal stability compared to bare iron oxide nanoparticles. This work demonstrates a sustainable strategy for valorizing silicon-rich semiconductor backgrinding waste into a magnetically recoverable nanocomposite with potential Fenton-like catalytic functionality, integrating pollutant removal and post-treatment magnetic separation.

item.title: Carexanes as Natural Ligands for a KRAS Promoter-Derived G-Quadruplex
item.description:
Abstract
Natural products represent a valuable source of structurally diverse scaffolds for the development of ligands targeting noncanonical nucleic acid structures, such as G-quadruplex (GQ). Herein, we investigated the binding properties of four natural compounds extracted from Mediterranean plants─distachyasin, carexane B, carexane C, and magnoflorine─toward the GQ formed by the KRAS22-RT sequence, a modified KRAS-derived oligonucleotide commonly used as a model of the KRAS oncogene, which adopts a single, well-defined parallel intramolecular GQ structure. Circular dichroism (CD), UV/Vis, and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopies were employed to investigate the interactions between KRAS22-RT GQ and the four compounds. Among them, carexane B exhibited the strongest stabilizing effect on KRAS22-RT GQ. Moreover, it showed a preliminary binding preference for the KRAS22-RT GQ, with no appreciable spectroscopic perturbation detected under the experimental conditions employed with either the GQ derived from the C9orf72 gene (Orf72 GQ) or the model DNA duplex (ds12) obtained from the Dickerson dodecamer. Finally, the preliminary in vitro biological activity of the four compounds was assessed in three breast cancer cell lines.

item.title: Trust in Machine Learning-Aided Docking: A Systematic Review of Good Practices for Chemically Reliable Predictions
item.description:
Abstract
The massive growth of chemical libraries presents both an opportunity and a challenge in large-scale virtual screening. Machine learning (ML) algorithms have successfully accelerated this process with surrogate docking models that learn patterns between molecular representations and docking scores for ranking undocked molecules. Deep learning (DL), which represents the majority of ML-boosted docking approaches, has a sophisticated capability of finding nonlinear, complex relationships in voluminous data. However, DL algorithms operate as black boxes, face difficulties in generalization and raise concerns on whether correct predictions are, in fact, made for causal relationships between chemical structure and biological activity. Candidate molecules cannot be confidently tested if predictions are not understandable in human terms. The lack of understanding of relevant chemical properties impairs compound discovery, optimization and novelty, reinforcing the high-risk and high-cost scenario of drug design. To offer insights for expanding the recent breakthroughs achieved with the docking/ML integration, this review included 57 ML-aided docking papers from January 2020 to August 2026. We assessed how ML predictions are generated, refined and chemically interpreted to reliably reduce docking simulations and ideally increase experimental hit rates by data-driven and expert-driven decisions on compound selection. On this matter, the proper implementation of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques is informative to elucidate if and how trustworthy are predicted hits from a chemical perspective, assuring a safer and more effective decision-making process for finding true hits. Nonetheless, only four (7.0%) out of 57 papers applied XAI techniques, mostly involving feature attribution methods, but not the state-of-the-art contrastive explanations method. Therefore, the implementation of XAI in ML-boosted docking is still scarce and needs formalization to avoid misinterpreting results. We review the various opportunities and limitations for integrating ML-aided docking with XAI techniques alongside complementary trust-enhancing strategies present in the included studies, such as sampling strategies, target diversity, ensemble and consensus docking, active learning, ensemble models, physicochemical and pharmacophore-based filtering, multiobjective optimization of molecular properties, confidence metrics of predefined acceptable errors, and expected model improvement along iterations. Given the broad applications of XAI across scientific domains and proof-of-concept studies in computational chemistry, we believe benchmarking and combining current and novel trust-enhancing strategies in ML-aided docking can go beyond finding initial hits. It supports both the statistical assessment including XAI in predictions and the mechanistic understanding of chemically relevant drug candidates for transparent and credible model and drug development.

item.title: Synthesis of Biographite from Starch Biomass Using Additive Assisted Templating Approach
item.description:
Abstract
Graphite is a critical mineral with wide-ranging applications in electronics, energy storage, and advanced materials manufacturing. As natural reserves remain limited, there is growing interest in using carbon-rich renewable precursors as alternative feedstocks for synthetic graphite production. Starch, being a widely available, renewable, and carbon-neutral biopolymer, is a compelling, sustainable alternative precursor for graphitic carbon synthesis. However, its inherently nongraphitizable nature requires templating additives to achieve graphitic ordering. In this study, we present a catalyst-free thermal route to produce graphitic carbon from starch-biopolymer-based packing peanuts through carbonization and graphitization, using graphene oxide (GO) and graphene (Gr) as templating additives. The resulting carbon structures were characterized using high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), selected area electron diffraction (SAED), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Raman spectroscopy to evaluate the improvements in crystallite parameters La and Lc. At the optimal condition of 2.5 wt % GO loading, crystallite parameters of La = 77.9 nm and Lc = 25.94 nm were achieved, closely approaching those of natural graphite (La = 100 nm, Lc = 24.6 nm). Oxygen content, edge-to-basal oxygen ratio, sp2 π-network, and stacking height are identified as the key factors governing the formation of graphitic or hard carbon from the starch precursor. Unlike conventional catalytic graphitization, this approach requires no metal catalysts, eliminating postprocessing purification entirely. The results establish starch biopolymer as a viable and sustainable precursor for graphitic carbon production.

item.title: A Practical Approach to Efficiency Calibration of an HPGe Gamma-Ray Spectrometer for Soil Matrix Measurements Using Reference Materials
item.description:
Abstract
In this study, a metrologically traceable and cost-effective efficiency calibration method for a coaxial HPGe gamma-ray spectrometer was developed using the IAEA–312 soil reference material and validated with the IAEA–447 moss-soil reference material. The efficiency curve was derived from selected gamma-ray lines of 214Pb and 214Bi in the energy range 242–1764 keV and fitted using a fourth-order logarithmic polynomial. The fitted model showed excellent agreement with the experimental data (R2 ≈ 0.996), with residuals within ±6%. The calibration was applied to determine the activity concentrations of 226Ra, 232Th, 137Cs, and 40K in IAEA–447. The measured values were in good agreement with the certified values, with relative deviations below 6% and all zeta-scores well below unity, indicating no statistically significant bias and confirming the traceability of the efficiency transfer. A comprehensive uncertainty analysis showed that the uncertainty in the efficiency calibration primarily determines overall accuracy, whereas counting statistics dominate for weaker gamma-ray lines. The results demonstrated that this approach provides a practical, matrix-matched calibration in which geometry-specific effects are inherently accounted for through empirical transfer and verified by reference material validation.

item.title: Retraction of “Cyanopyridinone- and Cyanopyridine-Based Cancer Cell Pim-1 Inhibitors: Design, Synthesis, Radiolabeling, Biodistribution, and Molecular Modeling Simulation”
item.description: The editor retracts “Cyanopyridinone- and Cyanopyridine-Based Cancer Cell Pim-1 Inhibitors: Design, Synthesis, Radiolabeling, Biodistribution, and Molecular Modeling Simulation” (DOI: 10.1021/acsomega.2c08304) due to inappropriate reuse of images from a prior publication and the unavailability of key raw data, undermining confidence in the reported results. Specifically, the mice imaging in the graphical abstract is duplicated from 10.2147/IJN.S325322, and raw data for the biodistribution study, MTT assay, and partial NMR data are unavailable. As such, the Article is being retracted.

item.title: Isatins: Historical Exploration, Sources, Biosynthetic Pathways, SAR, Biological Activities, Targeted Drug Delivery Systems, and Applications
item.description:
Abstract
Isatins have attracted significant interest from research groups worldwide due to their structural diversity, multifunctional biological activities, and medicinal properties. This review outlines the historical exploration of isatins, their synthetic and natural origins, biosynthetic pathways, structure–activity relationships (SAR), biological activities, targeted drug delivery systems, and applications. Based on data from various databases and publication societies, by the end of 2025, about 19 naturally occurring isatins have been reported and categorized into phenylpentyl-, prenyl-, halogenated-, hydroxy-, and sesquiterpenoid isatins. We also elucidated the intricate biosynthetic mechanisms underlying the formation of naturally derived isatins. We broadly and systematically outlined the SAR of isatins and reviewed their biological activities (anticancer, antimicrobial, antioxidant, antituberculosis, anti-inflammatory, anticonvulsant, anti-HIV). The review also covered the targeted drug delivery systems and applications of isatins.

item.title: Janus Bimodal Peptide Nucleic Acids (bm-PNA-C) n : pH-Controlled Assembly of i -Motif Tetraplexes and Fused bm-PNA:DNA Triple Duplexes
item.description:
Abstract
Our recent designs of Janus bimodal peptide nucleic acids (bm-PNA) have nucleobases attached to both sides of the aminoethylglycyl PNA backbone, equipping them for concurrent binding of two complementary DNA strands to form fused double duplexes. On the basis of the design of Janus PNA sequences, we have earlier shown that these form a variety of polyplexes ranging from double duplexes, triplex of duplexes, and tetraduplex of G4-tetraplexes. In this manuscript, we elaborate on this range to demonstrate Janus bm-PNA-Cn with cytosines attached to the PNA backbone via a flexible alkyl triazole linker, forming i-motif tetraplexes through C–H+···C at pH < 5.0, similar to the t-amide link as in standard PNA or via the glycosidic bond in DNA. At pH > 5.0, when cytosine N3 is nonprotonated, C:C duplexes occur by direct C:C base pairing from the triazole face. In such bm-PNA C:C self-duplexes, the mixed base sequence on two outer t-amide sides forms two duplexes with complementary DNA, leading to DNA:PNA-C:C-PNA:DNA triple duplexes, with synergistic stabilization of the constituent duplexes. The pH-dependent i-motif tetraplex (acidic pH) and triple duplexes (neutral pH) extend the repertoire of multistranded assemblies from Janus bm-PNAs. These open up future possibilities to build programmable functional supramolecular assemblies of multiplexes by tuning the sequences of both bm-PNA and DNA/RNA/PNA.

item.title: Facile Synthesis of Porous 2H-MoS 2 Nanoflowers for Highly Efficient Electrocatalytic Degradation of Azo Dye Eriochrome Black T
item.description:
Abstract
The extensive release of toxic azo dyes, particularly Eriochrome Black T (EBT), creates significant ecological and public health concerns. The development of efficient wastewater treatment technologies is therefore important for supporting the objectives of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), and SDG 13 (Climate Action). In this study, molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) nanoflowers synthesized using a single-step hydrothermal technique were used as high-performance electrodes for the electrochemical degradation of EBT. Comprehensive characterizations (FE-SEM, TEM, XRD, XPS, and FTIR) revealed the formation of a phase-pure 2H-MoS2 with an open, mesoporous structure of ultrathin nanosheets and a BET surface area of 10.54 m2 g–1. Systematic evaluation of the electrochemical parameters revealed that the MoS2 electrode achieved an excellent degradation efficiency of 100% within 90 min under optimized conditions (pH 3, applied voltage of 9 V, and initial dye concentrations of 30 and 50 ppm). The decolorization efficacy of the electrode was monitored using UV–visible spectrophotometry at 540 nm, while CV and LSV studies at varying concentrations confirmed efficient, concentration-dependent electrocatalytic oxidation. The degradation process followed pseudo-first-order kinetics at all temperatures. Mechanistic investigations using scavenger studies identified electro-generated holes (h+) as the primary reactive species driving oxidation. Furthermore, gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis of the degraded EBT solution confirmed the successful cleavage of the toxic azo (−N═N−) bonds and the progressive breakdown of complex aromatic rings into simpler aliphatic intermediates such as acetic acid. COD removal efficiency was found to be 81.8%. These results demonstrate the efficacy of MoS2 nanoflowers as potential electrocatalysts for wastewater treatment.

item.title: Phase Behavior and Separation Performance of Ethyl Lactate/Carbohydrate or Salt ATPS for Cypermethrin, Amoxicillin, and 17β-Estradiol
item.description:
Abstract
We evaluated aqueous biphasic systems (ATPS) based on ethyl lactate formed with sodium salts or carbohydrates as green liquid–liquid extractants for representative pollutants─cypermethrin, amoxicillin, and 17β-estradiol (E2). Solubility curves and tie lines were determined at 298.15 K to map phase behavior. Partitioning occurs preferentially into the ethyl lactate-rich phase, K = 10.24 ± 0.1 (EE = 95.13 ± 0.8%) for cypermethrin, K = 6.83 ± 0.6 (EE = 93.15 ± 0.7%) for amoxicillin, and K = 11.42 ± 0.3 (EE = 92.37 ± 0.3%) for E2 in the system containing 35 wt % ethyl lactate + 40 wt % Na2SO4. A 100-fold concentration factor was achieved in 58.2% (w/w) Na2SO4 + 6.2% (w/w) ethyl lactate (TLL = 86.4), enabling enhanced detection of trace pollutants. Phase formation was correlated with the salting-out effect and the stereochemistry of carbohydrates (equatorial −OH groups), and the effects of the salts’ hydration free energy were discussed. The results demonstrate a biocompatible and operationally simple route for the preconcentration of priority micropollutants, supporting integration with analytical monitoring and water treatment processes.

item.title: Malachite Green and Methyl Violet Adsorption by High-Silica Fly Ash-Based Materials: Comparison of Alkali-Fusion-hydrothermal and SDS-Assisted Surface Modification
item.description:
Abstract
High-silica fly ash was converted into a mesoporous high-silica fly ash-based material (MHS) through alkali-fusion-hydrothermal treatment and an alkyl-modified high-silica fly ash-based material (AMHS) through SDS-assisted surface modification. This study aimed to compare the effects of these two modification routes on the adsorption of malachite green (MG) and methyl violet (MV). Batch experiments identified an adsorbent dosage of 2 g L–1 and an equilibrium time of 180 min for both materials under the investigated conditions. MG adsorption by both MHS and AMHS was better described by the Langmuir model, whereas MV adsorption was better described by the Freundlich model. The Langmuir-derived maximum adsorption capacities of MHS for MG and MV were 85.32 and 67.20 mg g–1, respectively, while those of AMHS were 98.33 and 95.33 mg g–1, respectively. Binary-dye experiments indicated that MHS preferentially adsorbed MG, whereas AMHS exhibited comparable affinities toward MG and MV. The combined adsorption and characterization results suggest that the performance of MHS was associated primarily with its accessible mesoporous structure, while that of AMHS reflected the influence of SDS-assisted surface modification and accessible surface sites.

item.title: Chitosan-Based Palmarosa Essential Oil Nanoemulsion: Formulation, Characterization and Enhanced Larvicidal Activity against Culex Quinquefasciatus
item.description:
Abstract
Rising multigenerational resistance in Culex quinquefasciatus underscores the need for safer, more sustainable control methods. Cymbopogon martini (palmarosa) essential oil (PEO) repels insects, yet high volatility and limited stability restrict field use. To address these limitations, we developed a chitosan-loaded palmarosa oil nanoemulsion (CPN) to improve stability and larvicidal performance. Chemical profiling identified geraniol (67.6%) as the primary bioactive component. FTIR spectroscopy verified entrapment within the chitosan matrix, while DSC thermograms showed greater thermal stability with an endothermic peak at 57.52 °C. TEM, XRD, and DLS provided complementary structural confirmation of CPN stability. In larvicidal testing, CPN (LC50 = 22.515 ppm) proved markedly more potent than bulk PEO (LC50 = 124.466 ppm) within 24 h. Histological review of CPN-treated larvae revealed severe internal damage, including foregut tissue disintegration, myofibrillar fragmentation in thoracic muscles, and extensive fat body vacuolation. Gene-expression analysis indicated time-dependent upregulation of a protein kinase gene (PKA000798; ∼1.0-fold) and induction of an ER degradation gene (LOC6038600; ∼0.5–0.55-fold). Acute toxicity testing in zebrafish (Danio rerio) under OECD Guideline 203 showed no mortality at 100 mg/L, suggesting low acute toxicity under the tested conditions. Overall, these results present chitosan-encapsulated palmarosa oil as an effective, eco-friendly larvicide with minimal impact on nontarget organisms.

item.title: Stress Adaptation in Mycobacteria through Reprogramming of the Transcription–Translation Axis
item.description:
Abstract
Mycobacteria are highly resilient species with an extraordinary ability to survive a range of stresses and antibiotics, making it difficult to treat mycobacterial infections. This challenge is particularly apparent in the months-long treatment of tuberculosis, which is caused by infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis and kills over a million people every year worldwide. Over the last two decades, a significant body of knowledge has emerged on mechanisms employed by mycobacteria to survive under host-relevant stresses. However, only recently have we begun to appreciate the interconnectivity of these responses, often linked to shared transcriptional regulatory networks. While reviewing the literature, we highlight here the interlinkage in various stress responses in mycobacteria with particular focus on stress-induced regulation of transcription and translation pathways.

item.title: Mechanism and Coordinated Control Technology for Large Deformations of Deep Roadway under High Mining Stress: A Case Study
item.description:
Abstract
Deep roadways under high mining stress suffer remarkable asymmetric deformation and severe floor heave. Support failure mainly arises from inadequate consideration of asymmetric deformation and stability interactions among surrounding rock zones. To address large deformation control of deep roadways under high mining stress, this study investigates the roof–rib–floor coordinated control mechanism and technology via theoretical analysis, numerical simulation, and field tests. The results show that high mining stress, soft rock mass, and absent floor support dominate the deformation and failure of the 1103 roadway. Enhancing roof–rib support strength mitigates floor deformation and plastic zone depth, while strengthened floor support reduces rib deformation and plastic zone depth. Stable floor and ribs further improve roof stability. A roof–rib–floor coordinated support technology is proposed by integrating roof–rib hierarchical support and grouted floor cable bundles. For the roof and ribs, short and long cables construct a hierarchical support structure with strong shallow and weak deep reinforcement to achieve mechanical coupling between supports and surrounding rock. For the floor, high-strength cable bundles combined with grouting reinforcement improve deformation resistance. The corresponding control parameters for the 1103 roadway are determined and verified by field tests. The proposed theory and technology offer references for surrounding rock control of deep roadways under high mining stress.

item.title: New Polyneolignans from Nothotsuga longibracteata Growing in China
item.description:
Abstract
Four new polyneolignans (1–4) along with two known lignans were isolated from the heartwood of Nothotsuga longibracteata. Their structures were elucidated by high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (HR-ESIMS), together with spectroscopic methods including 1D/2D-NMR. Subsequent ECD computational analysis was further applied to confirm the stereochemistry of the undescribed polyneolignans. The plausible MS/MS fragmentation pathways of compounds 1 and 4 were proposed based on data acquired via electrospray ionization in negative ion mode. The summarized fragmentation rules facilitate the preliminary screening of analogous lignan constituents in botanical samples. Their cytotoxic activities against three cell lines (A172, SH-SY5Y, and HeLa) were evaluated using the 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay. Compound 2 exhibited a mild inhibitory effect against A172 cells, with an IC50 value of 25.97 μM.

item.title: Sustainable Alumina/Silk Fibroin Hybrid Dielectrics for Low-Temperature Fabrication of Flexible Organic Electronics
item.description:
Abstract
The transition toward sustainable organic electronics requires fabrication processes with reduced thermal budgets together with the integration of eco-compatible functional materials. Here, we report a sustainable hybrid dielectric platform based on low-temperature atomic layer deposition (ALD) of aluminum oxide (Al2O3) combined with silk fibroin (SF), a naturally derived protein, for flexible organic field-effect transistors (OFETs). An 80 °C ALD process was developed to deposit Al2O3 layers directly on flexible polyethylene naphthalate (PEN), chosen as a model mechanically compliant and thermally sensitive substrate. To engineer the dielectric/semiconductor interface, ultrathin SF layers were deposited on Al2O3 and compared with poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) as the synthetic benchmark. Morphological, dielectric, electrical and mechanical investigations show that SF forms continuous films on low-temperature ALD Al2O3 and supports a semiconductor morphology comparable to that obtained on PMMA-buffered interfaces. OFETs incorporating Al2O3/SF hybrid dielectrics operate at gate voltages below 20 V with low leakage currents and carrier mobilities of the order of 1 cm2 V–1 s–1, and retain field-effect operation at a bending radius of 5 mm. Remarkably, this is achieved with as-cast SF, whereas PMMA requires a prolonged thermal treatment. Combining low-temperature oxide processing with natural biopolymers, this platform offers a route toward sustainable, biobased and eco-compatible organic electronics.

item.title: Structure–Activity Relationship of N-(2-(Piperidin-1-yl)phenyl)benzene-1,4-disulfonamides as TRPML1 Agonists
item.description:
Abstract
Transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) is a lysosomal Ca2+ channel that regulates lysosomal trafficking, autophagy, and membrane repair. Its pharmacological activation represents a promising strategy for treating lysosomal dysfunction-related diseases, including lysosomal storage disorders, neurodegenerative diseases, muscular dystrophies, infectious diseases, and inflammatory disorders. However, existing TRPML1 agonists suffer from limitations that restrict their utility as in vivo probes and therapeutic leads. We report a comprehensive structure–activity relationship (SAR) study of N-(2-(piperidin-1-yl)phenyl)benzene-1,4-disulfonamides that delivered potent, selective, and pharmacokinetically improved TRPML1 agonists. Systematic scaffold optimization revealed key structural determinants of channel activation, yielding substantial potency gains alongside improved physicochemical, metabolic, and pharmacokinetic properties. Refinement of the aryl sulfonamide substituents and piperidine-containing moieties established clear SAR trends that enhanced cellular activity. Lead compounds exhibited robust TRPML1 agonism, high selectivity over related TRP channels, and in vivo-compatible pharmacokinetics. These studies validate this scaffold as a privileged chemotype for TRPML1 activation, providing optimized chemical probes for investigating TRPML1 biology and a foundation for therapeutic development across multiple indications.

item.title: Design of Sustainable Formulations for Nanodosing: Insight into Fatty Acid Profile Modulation in Tenebrio molitor Larvae
item.description:
Abstract
In the context of sustainable insect production,Tenebrio molitor larvae (TML) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional livestock systems. Their rich nutritional profile is characterized by high protein content and favorable lipid composition. Herein, we developed nanovectors based on exopolysaccharides derived from Neocyanospira capsulata(Es) or olive pomace (O), combined with egg yolk phospholipids (E) to deliver oils obtained from the seeds ofPerilla frutescens L. (Britt.) (Pf) andSclerocarya birrea (A.Rich.) (Sb) as a dietary supplement in TML. These oils differ significantly in their lipid composition: Pf presents high levels of C18:3 n-3, whose increase may be desirable in TML, while Sb has a considerable amount of C18:1 n-9, along with relatively higher proportions of C16:0 and C18:0. Both plain and oil-loaded nanovectors were characterized by dynamic light scattering (DLS), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and ζ-potential to obtain size distribution, shape, and surface charge. The oils were administered to TML through nanovectors at an extremely low dose of 3.15 nL per larva per day, and their effect on the fatty acid profile was investigated. Results showed that Pf-nanovectors increased C18:3 n-3 in treated larvae, whereas the free oil emulsion administered at the same dose did not produce comparable effects. All oil-loaded nanovectors altered the relative proportions of saturated fatty acids and monounsaturated fatty acids compared to the control treatments, suggesting that encapsulated lipids modulate larval lipid metabolism. All these findings support the potential of nanovectors as low-dose delivery systems for modulating the lipid composition of TML.

item.title: Activating Interlayer Organic Redox Sites in Hybrid Layered Vanadium Oxides for Li-Ion Batteries via Dopamine-Derived Carbonization
item.description:
Abstract
Chemical preintercalation of redox-active organic molecules can enhance the specific capacity of layered metal oxides by introducing interlayer redox sites alongside intralayer redox centers. However, their practical redox activity in hybrid electrodes is often limited due to sluggish charge transport kinetics. Here, we show that dopamine (DOPA) carbonization activates 2,6-diaminoanthraquinone (DAAQ) molecules in bilayered vanadium oxide (BVO) hybrid electrodes, resulting in notable capacity improvement in nonaqueous Li-ion cells. BVO preintercalated solely with DAAQ (DAAQ-100) is compared with BVO preintercalated with both DAAQ and DOPA, followed by DOPA carbonization (DAAQ-65/DOPA). We found that DOPA carbonization competes with DAAQ preintercalation, reducing the interlayer DAAQ fraction while increasing hydration, yet preserving hydrogen-bond cross-linking between DAAQ and V–O layers, which enhances structural stability. Notably, DAAQ-65/DOPA exhibits a unique nanoscroll morphology, in contrast to the nanobelt morphology of DAAQ-100. Transmission electron microscopy suggests formation of interlayer carbon domains in DAAQ-65/DOPA and cyclic voltammetry indicates that DOPA-derived carbon domains activate interlayer DAAQ redox sites and enhance vanadium redox activity, which is attributed to improved charge transfer. Consequently, DAAQ-65/DOPA delivers a high initial specific capacity of ∼240 mAh g–1 at 20 mA g–1 and improved rate capability of ∼160 mAh g–1 at 200 mA g–1, outperforming DAAQ-100. Electrochemical analysis, supported by galvanostatic intermittent titration (GITT) and Nyquist plots, reveals fast charge transport kinetics arising from enhanced electron and Li+ mobility. This study demonstrates, for the first time, that DOPA carbonization can activate interlayer organic redox sites in hybrid electrodes, offering a new strategy to enhance energy storage performance.

item.title: Construction of Chloromethyl Esters from Carboxylic Acids Using Bromochloromethane and Further Transformation to Nitrate Esters
item.description:
Abstract
A method for the synthesis of chloromethyl esters from carboxylic acids and bromochloromethane was developed. The reaction, utilizing Cs2CO3 and bromochloromethane, exhibited a broad substrate scope, encompassing aromatic, aliphatic, and heteroaromatic compounds; natural products; and medicinal drugs. The system was extended to the production of nitrate esters from chloromethyl esters and silver nitrate.

item.title: 3,4-Bis(benzyloxy)benzaldehyde-Derived Hydrazones: Synthesis, α-Amylase-Selective Inhibition, Antioxidant Profiling, and In Silico Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
Carbohydrate-hydrolyzing enzymes (α-amylase and α-glucosidase) are clinically validated targets for controlling postprandial hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and oxidative stress is a recognized contributor to disease progression. Herein, a series of hydrazone Schiff bases derived from 3,4-bis(benzyloxy)benzaldehyde were synthesized by acid-catalyzed condensation of the aldehyde with para-substituted phenylhydrazines and were characterized by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy, FT-IR spectroscopy, and high-resolution mass spectrometry; chromatographic purity was established by RP-HPLC (94.5–98.6 area % at 350 nm). The series was evaluated for in vitro inhibition of porcine pancreatic α-amylase and yeast α-glucosidase and for antioxidant capacity using four complementary assays (DPPH, ABTS, FRAP, and CUPRAC). The compounds displayed a pronounced α-amylase preference: compound 9 (IC50 = 160.40 ± 2.05 μg/mL) and compound 7 (IC50 = 166.01 ± 2.64 μg/mL) were the most potent and exceeded acarbose under the assay conditions (IC50 = 232.66 ± 4.93 μg/mL); on a molar basis, both are essentially equipotent with the reference drug (345.2 ± 4.4 and 378.6 ± 6.0 μM versus 360.4 ± 7.6 μM), and IC50 values are reported in both units throughout (Table 1). α-Glucosidase inhibition was moderate, with the para-chloro analogue 3 being the most active (IC50 = 83.13 ± 6.53 μg/mL; 187.7 ± 14.7 μM). The selectivity index (IC50 α-glucosidase/IC50 α-amylase) spans 0.22 for 3 to 2.38 for 9, so a single para-substituent determines which carbohydrase is preferred. Antioxidant behavior was assay-dependent: compounds 1 and 4 delivered the highest ferric-reducing power (FRAP = 1854.0 ± 1.5 and 1786.7 ± 5.2 μmol Fe2+/g), and compound 5 gave the strongest CUPRAC response (280.95 ± 3.43 mg GAE/g). Molecular docking against α-amylase (PDB 1B2Y) and α-glucosidase (PDB 3TOP), together with SwissADME, QikProp, and ADMETlab profiling, provides a structural rationale for the observed substituent effects. These results define a clear, substituent-driven selectivity relationship within a lipophilic dibenzyloxy hydrazone framework and establish the DBZO-hydrazone scaffold as a tractable system for further optimization.

item.title: In Silico Identification of Peptide Pharmacophoric Determinants and Complementary Binding Hotspots on Fungal Grr1
item.description:
Abstract
The growing burden of human and plant fungal diseases, compounded by limited therapeutic options and emerging antifungal resistance, underscores the need to identify novel molecular targets for antifungal intervention. In this context, the fungal F-box protein Grr1 acts as the substrate-recognition component of the SCF ubiquitin ligase complex, binding phosphorylated degrons to direct substrate degradation and regulate key cellular processes. However, the structural and energetic determinants governing phosphodegron recognition by the Grr1 leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain remain poorly characterized. Here, we investigated the molecular basis of Grr1 recognition of phosphodegrons derived from the substrates Cln2 and Gic2 and evaluated whether phosphomimetic substitutions could preserve their interaction with the LRR domain. Structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, binding free-energy calculations, per-residue energy decomposition, and pharmacophore modeling were integrated to characterize the Grr1-degron interfaces and identify their major recognition determinants. Phosphorylation was required to maintain stable association of both degrons with the concave surface of the Grr1 LRR domain. Per-residue energy analysis revealed a conserved basic recognition surface comprising Arg418, Arg496, Lys498, Arg550, Lys608, Arg680, and Arg709, with Lys498, Arg550, Arg680, and Arg709 emerging as the principal energetic contributors shared by both complexes. Together, these residues form an electropositive environment that coordinates the degron phosphate groups, while pharmacophore mapping identified complementary molecular features associated with ligand recognition. Remarkably, substitution of the phosphorylated residues with aspartate preserved the calculated binding free energy of both degrons, whereas glutamate substitution disrupted stable binding, indicating that phosphomimetic recognition depends not merely on negative charge but critically on its precise spatial positioning within the recognition interface. Collectively, these findings define a conserved structural and energetic mechanism of phosphodegron recognition by fungal Grr1 and identify molecular features that can be exploited for ligand development. This framework supports the rational design of phosphomimetic peptides and other competitive ligands targeting the Grr1 substrate-recognition interface and provides a foundation for exploring this conserved regulatory system as a potential strategy for antifungal intervention.

item.title: Reactive-Extruded PLA/PBAT/Bentonite Nanocomposites for Diffusion-Controlled Urea Release in Sustainable Fertilizer Systems
item.description:
Abstract
Approximately 70% of conventional fertilizers applied to soil are lost to the environment, mainly through leaching, especially in sandy and organic soils. This inefficiency increases environmental impact and reduces nutrient use efficiency. Controlled-release fertilizers (CRFs) have emerged as a viable strategy to regulate nutrient availability over time. In this context, biodegradable polymers are promising coating materials due to their ability to degrade gradually in soil. Blends based on poly(lactic acid) (PLA) and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) have been investigated; however, their thermodynamic immiscibility compromises interfacial adhesion and overall performance. To overcome this limitation, in situ reactive extrusion was employed using maleic anhydride as a grafting agent and dicumyl peroxide as an initiator, aiming to enhance phase compatibility. Additionally, the fully organomodified bentonite clay was incorporated as a functional filler and urea adsorbent. PLA/PBAT (70/30 wt %) system containing 2 phr maleic anhydride, 1 phr dicumyl peroxide, and 3 wt % bentonite was processed under different screw speeds and feed rates to determine the optimal conditions of processing. The composites were characterized in terms of thermal behavior, morphology, and water absorption. The optimal formulation, obtained at lower screw speed and higher feed rate, exhibited improved physicochemical properties. A CRF was produced by adding 10 wt % of urea to the optimized system. Leaching tests demonstrated gradual nutrient release, with a maximum released fraction 20.7% lower than that of the PLA/PBAT/urea system without bentonite clay, confirming the positive effect of bentonite on nutrient retention and controlled-release performance.

item.title: Bioinspired Melanin Coatings Generated by Artificial Manganese Metalloenzymes for Sustainable Hair Pigmentation
item.description:
Abstract
The design of next-generation hair colorants is progressively moving toward bioinspired methodologies that reproduce natural melanogenesis under environmentally benign and mild reaction conditions. Among these approaches, catalysts displaying catecholase-mimicking behavior have attracted considerable interest as sustainable substitutes for conventional oxidative dyeing systems, owing to their capacity to induce melanin formation while reducing structural damage to hair fibers. Motivated by the multifunctional nature of melanin in living organisms, where it acts not only as a pigment but also as a UV-screening and antioxidant material; herein, we describe a chemoenzymatic strategy for the in situ deposition of synthetic melanin-like coatings on human hair through Mn-based artificial metalloenzymes. The catalytic system is based on colloidal manganese nanoparticle–enzyme hybrids engineered to exhibit oxidase-like activity. Manganese was selected due to its abundance, low toxicity, cost-effectiveness, and advantageous physicochemical characteristics. Notably, the incorporation of surfactants during hybrid preparation markedly improved both catalytic efficiency and thermal robustness, affording highly active metalloenzymatic assemblies capable of rapidly oxidizing dopamine and triggering polymerization within minutes under aqueous, base-free conditions at ambient temperature. This biomimetic process enables localized melanin generation directly on hair fibers, resulting in homogeneous, tunable, and natural-appearing coloration with excellent resistance to repeated washing and thermal exposure. In addition to cosmetic pigmentation, the deposited melanin-like layers may impart supplementary protective properties, including enhanced UV blocking and mitigation of photoinduced damage. Collectively, these findings introduce a sustainable platform for multifunctional hair dyeing and demonstrate the potential of Mn-derived artificial metalloenzymes in advanced cosmetic and surface-coating technologies.
